To be honest. This game needs a LOT of work. I was pretty excited for this game too, but sadly the game just has too much working against it and it tends to ruin the experience for me. Pretty much, every issue stated in other "Not Reccomended" reviews are completely, and sadly, correct.
The mechanics of the game works like this; You train for fights, the skills degrade every day, you fight, and in between that time you try to do everything to not go hungry. That would mean that you must work. Then you have to also monitor a; romantic relationship, pit fights, bar fights, being a super hero, and every-other thing outside of the basic mechanics of the game. Sounds great in concept, too bad it is poorly excecuted.
The main gripe, and the one that would fix a ton of these issues, is the skill degration. It is brutal and combine that with all the extra-cirricular things that you need to do and somehow manage to not go hungry, and you can imagine how dishearteningly grindy this game is. You work to try to get your skills up, well good luck with that; if you're hungy/tired, you need to stop, if you are low on money you need to stop, if you need food you need to stop, if you want a romantic relationship you need to stop, if you want to be a super hero you need to stop. All these things slows down your ability to train. But don't worry, the minute a day passes, you loose half of all the stats you've tried to gain beforehand.
It becomes a depressing fight upstream to even get decent skills in this game. You can't really progress to the fun bits when you're having to deal with this soul-crushing uphill battle. This, sadly, becomes worse when you have to deal with the actual "fights".
I say "fights" as there really aren't fights you can totally control. I get the idea behind it, but the strategy goes out the window when your higher stat fighter, proceeds to just stand there and take punch after punch, and kick after kick.  And it's not like this happens every once in a while. It happens in every fight. Honestly, I would rather just have control over my avatar. Either that or just not have the fight portion and just act like the cornerman/head trainer and just give strategy/instructions to the avatar. I don't know how many times I had rage-quitted this game because of the fact that my avatar would not do a damned thing while I just sat there yelling at him to do anything other than take punches/kicks to the face! Again, this would just have been alliviated if the player had control over the character.
Again, it's not like I hate this game. In fact, I really want to like it. The art style and the vibe of the game would make this a pretty fun game. Sadly, it's like this game is fighting me every step of the way to make me like this game. It needs to be patched, but I sadly don't see them making one anytime soon. I guess that means that this game is going to be gathering virtual dust in my Steam library.
If I wanted to end this review with something for any reader to remember, I guess I would say to not get this game. It's depressing. It's depressing in how the mechanics just suck the life out of a potentially fun game experience, and it's depressing in how you have very little control over the more important part of the game, the fighting.
Difficult to describe and with weird mechanics, the only thing I can say is that it's awesome.

I first played this on the PS2 and loved it. It was the "Rogue Squadron" of the PS2; although, having played RS myself, they're just similar in that they are both flight games - that's it. Does that mean it's bad? No. The flight combat mechanics are quite smooth and the gameplay is quite fast. It's great in its owy way. I recommend that you use a gamepad for this game (it even recognizes an Xbox 360 controller!).
As for the story, it's setting during Episode I, although it's focused on characters that weren't in the movies. You play as Rhys Dallows (a Naboo fighter pilot with the familiar N-1 fighter), Vana Sage (a mercenary with the Guardian Mantis) and Nym (a pirate with the Havoc bomber). The characters are likable and it's a shame the story wasn't long enough to spend time with them (it's just less than 6 hours). But you also have bonus missions and you can replay the story missions with different craft (e.g. flying the N-1 fighter on Nym's missions instead of his Havoc).
Given the low price, I recommend this game if you like space or flight action games, and even more if you're a Star Wars fan.

tl;dr ver
Gameplay:
The pacing in assassins creed III isn’t normalized, new features and part of the maps are introduced to the player in a manner where you are overwhelmed with side quests and other things to do. This may kill the understanding of the player of what the story is really trying to tell. It doesn’t help also that the missions in the early parts of the game are held in the winter, heavy snow slows everything down.
They tried to add new weapons and tools, but it didn’t hook me enough to actually use them frequently. The UI is also consolized as usual, but one thing I really hate is the weapon UI. You can only bind up to 4 things and if you want to switch to other tools, you need to bring up the whole UI, pausing the game before you can access your weapons.
Despite of that, features improved parkouring (you can now parkour in trees in the jungle), Stealth gameplay is also improved (a little bit buggy still), combat is also a little bit harder with the new combo and counter system.
Graphics and performance:
The maps are beautifully made, with 3 massive maps and numerous smaller maps to roam, there are tons of content in this game. The forest looks amazing with the number of trees, obstacle, details and the wildlife in them. Textures are incredibly mediocre when you look at them in short distances with the exception on the outside maps (not inside animus)
Performance was disappointing, crossfire/SLI was not supported or badly scales. In-fact, my crossfire setup had negative scaling when CF is on. FPS is horrible in some parts of boston. The game was obviously CPU bound since my performance increased a lot when I switch my Phenom II AMD processor to an i7.
Final thoughts
Overall, I think the game was just rushed and wasn't ready to be released. This is very apparent since most of the things are unpolished and filled with bugs.

Having binged on all of the AC games, back to back, a couple of months ago, I felt compelled to write a review about this one. I have to say AC3 is one of the weakest entries in the series, and although it has some very good qualities, they are not enough to redeem the game as a whole. First and foremost, the story feels like it underwent heavy cuts in all the wrong places. There are parts of the game that literally advance oon a very slow pace, with mundane actions that, unlike in the Ezio games, do not offer any insight into the characters or, if they do, the characters are often too uninteresting to relate to. The way they implemented the main character into the actual history is also all kinds of messed up; he was basically everywhere, and he single-handedly won the War of American Independence.
Another problem I found very anoying was the controls. They are the same sort of sticky controls as in previous iterations, but I found that for some reason the character never seems to go where you want him to, and just tries to stick-climb to the nearest surface. This is VERY annoying when the game itself demands precision. After a while I just gave up trying to do the tasks needed for full sync, since they felt more like a chore rather than fun (AC4, on the other hand, did these full sync tasks right). Also, don't get fooled by the trailers that look like they promise huge battles and freedom in the way you may tackle them. Your participation in both of the big battles that appear in the game is very linear and unsatisfying. This is true for most of the main story missions as well, which basically amount to: follow this guy, listen to conversation, kill a bunch of guys, run away.
Now, all is not bad: the graphics are good, pc optimization is alright, and some of the side missions are actually pretty interesting (building the homestead, for example). The best part of the game for me was, undoubtedly, the naval missions, which are regretably only a handful (at least it felt like it, since they were so much fun). I'd dare say I even found the controls and feel of the sailing a bit better than in AC4; the weight of the ship factors strongly, and it's not so easy to steer as in the latter, which felt a bit too arcade-y for my liking. Still, I find AC4 to be the best of the bunch, and would recommend it strongly over any of the others, followed by the also fantastic Ezio trilogy. AC3, on the other hand, fell flat on expectations and is the worst game in the series, only after the first one, which hasn't aged well at all.
PD: I also finished the DLCs which, I have to say, are even worst than the main game. They focus strongly on combat, making you fight a ♥♥♥♥-ton of soldiers even for the ♥♥♥♥♥iest of rewards. Want to open a chest? ♥♥♥♥ you, fight 50 guys. Want to talk to Ben Franklin? ♥♥♥♥ you, fight 50 guys. Want to walk down the street? ♥♥♥♥ you, fight 50 guys. I'm not even joking, even the smallest encounter feels like you just killed half the population of colonial America. This is the worst kind of dlc: pure, unfiltered filler. And infurating as hell, I get riled up even thinking about it. Avoid at ALL costs.

You can die, which requires you to start all the way over. You can shoot people and change out weapons during a race. There's also crazy drug races where cars are just flying all over the place.
The biggest complaint I have is that the actually racing and feel to the bikes are way off. There's little regard to real physics not gravity in the game. The races use a rubber band method to attach each other side-by-side so you easy bust face with bat. And while that's fine, Road Rash was always a blast because you're have to maintain your speed to side-by-side. It never just locked you into that place to attack.
My overall recommendation is to wait this one out until it's final, unless you see a cheap deal.

This NOT a GTA clone by Ubisoft. The game has very likeable main characters and really cool missions. There are lots of different ways to be creative in your way of solving problems in this game. You can blow up steam pipes and the police Don't know that it is you. The multiplayer is also fun because you have to detect the enemy.

People will hate me for saying this, but i enjoy this game more than i did Grand Theft Auto V. To be fair Watch_Dog2 came out years later, so this game had enough time to build upon the GTA formula. The graphics of this game has its own subtle feel to it, where its not better graphically than gta, but stand out enough to have a better graphical presentation compared to GTAV.
My biggest peeve about modern open world games is the lack of environmental interaction. This game does what GTAV doesn't and that offers advance environmental interaction along with a simple to basic cover base system. In a shoot out against enemies, dont expect pray and spray mechanics, which is satisfyingly common in cover base shooters.
Watch dog 2 allows you to approach missions in different ways, finding key areas to exploit enough to complete the mission in a stealthy way or just go ball to the wall crazy and shoot everything. I played the game on realistic mode, so a few shots from enemies and you die instantly. This level of difficulty is the optimum way of playing the game, which from dying a couple of times from the same mission and finally beating it gives you a satisfying feel of accomplishment.
The game is full of a couple of mini games, which again i enjoy more so than your average GTA series filler mini games. some were boring in watch dog, some weren't. I just wish they added the cliche car racing mini game we are far too familiar with. speaking of cars, dont expect to see a ton of different varieties of races. i've felt like i seen the same type of  racers over and over and over again, more so than in GTAV.
The Peds in this game has a ton of nice AI and its full of randomness, again far better than GTAV. You'd see random ped walk up to an ex and slap them. you'll see random group fights. I witness a all out huge cops vs gang fight that took over a whole neighborhood, which i then had to flee for my life. Pure randomness of this game is what i expect from certain other open world game. Its so random, that i sometimes felt like i was watching an encounter from the game The Sims.
I recommend this game to anyone. Don't play it for the story, play it for the experience. Its a pretty nice game and has so much potential.

Okay. I'm going to Siskel & Ebert this thing. (If you're old enough to catch most the references in this game, you're old enough to catch the one I just made, LOL) I LOVE IT!! And..I hate it also, LOL
What's good? Storyline is cool. Retro vibes are cool. The stregeic sim value is cool, though deeply flawed. (More on that later.) The music is cool. Unlike others, I see the value of the way the sim system is set up...mostly. It's like a chess game planning out your life between eating, sleeping, earning money, and training. In other words, it is the Ultimate Amateur Hardcore Life Sim, LOL
Unfortunately, that's also the problem. It acts like a micro-transaction game in a lot of ways. It's unbalanced as hell. (I had my fighter up to 3/2/3 and got my♥♥♥♥♥kicked by a 1/1/1. >_>) I also don't like the fact that they make it appear as though the bus system is to help you from getting robbed, and yet...it doesn't do shizz for that. :/ In other words, the bus concept is pointless. Another issue I have is that the pot is coerced with the illusion of choice. All roads lead to Rome in this game. No matter what option you chose (for the most part) the end result is exactly the same.
In fact, I would say that this sim is micro-transaction style on crack. At least in a traditional micro-transaction game your stats regenerate over time. You plummet stats in here, without money, food, Mick, or energy, you are royally screed in Spades. At least in a micro-transaction game, even if the stats didn't regenerate, if I was desperate enough I could buy my way out of a jam. Not here. :/
Also don't like the mini-encounters. Particularly the briefcase. I go home to get some sleep, and next thing I know, that damn briefcase is sending me god knows where to a fight I didn't plan on fighting. The game also punishes you for making money instead of buffing stats. I let my stats drop to get cash to get equipment to make training easier and less expensive, and next fight I have is against Roy who had triple to six times my stats. That has NEVER happened before, because in previous games I never let my stats drop.
Also, piece of advice; despite Mick's proclomation he will feed you, he's a stingy s.o.b. His meals fill you by half if you're lucky, and he's a 'three strikes and you're out' kind of guy. Literally, he will ONLY feed you 3x.
Overall, I LOVE the game, seriously. Yes, it is brutal. Yes, it's often not fair. But neither is life. I agree with previous reviewers who are irritated people are down voting the game because it's difficult. But I agree it needs tweaked in some major areas as well. But then again, I expect that from a game in progress.
Last complaint...the constant updating. This too, is something I love and hate, LOL It happens because the developers are listening. But damn it gets annoying having two updates five minutes apart like happened to me today, LOL
In the end, however, I MUST give Punch Club a rather enthusiastic thumbs...UP. Fun game, yes frustrating, but not so much that I have cause to hate it. Just cause for complaint, LOL

I have been a huge fan of the AC series and have legitimately enjoyed every single game except for the Chronicle games. I have been known to be leniant toward the series about things that a lot of other people are usually much harsher about. Here's why I am absolutely loving AC Origins so far. It is completely and 100% seamless, where the only loading screens (that are pretty short on a HDD btw) are when you fast travel and going in and coming out of cutscenes. Unlike in the previous games where there's a loading screen anytime you leave a city and such, this game has none of that. The size of the world and the seamlessness reminds me of the Witcher 3's world. The controls are a bit confusing at first because they changed it from the previous games so veterans of the series might be put off at first HOWEVER there is an alternate control scheme that is basically classic AC controls. The modern era stuff, which a lot of people dislike, is very minor like in AC Unity and Syndicate. Hunting and wildlife is a lot more immersive and well done compared to AC 3 and Black Flag. There is microtransactions in the game HOWEVER they are actually completely unnecessary and a nonfactor in the game, you can get any outfit, money, etc. all on your own in the game at a reasonable pace. MT's are there, but please do not let that deter you, because you definitely don't need them. This also seems to be one of the best optimized games in the series as well. I have a 1080Ti and an Intel i7 Quad Core and at max settings I get straight 60 FPS. Your mileage may vary obviously if you have a weaker system but from first glance and the amount of possible graphics options available in the settings, it is very much optimised well, way better than Unity, Syndicate, and even Black Flag. Also, for those who care about Steam achievements, its also the first AC game to have Steam achievements which is nice.
If I had one complaint about the game so far, is that like previous games, in the beginning parts of the world are block by story progression. It doesn't last long, but its there. If I were to give it an arbitrary score out of 10, it'd be 9/10.
EDIT: I forgot to mention, but another major plus is that they have gotten rid of optional objectives, allowing for much more freedom with missions and much less frustrations. However they have also gotten rid of the memory sequence system, where you could replay missions and the like.
EDIT #2: Do not sit on this game. It really is THE best in the series and that's from someone who already loves the series.

I'm going to make this review short, because there's so much content in the game that I made the experience so long. I mean, there's a lot of stuff to do. A LOT.
Okay, so the story wasn't the high point; Connor is an angsty teenager who's one a revenge quest for the death of his mother and the burning of his village. While his goals are similar to that of the Sons of Liberty, that is, when he meets them, he's careless and anxious. I praise Ubisoft for getting the character of an overly anxious youth correct, but his weakness is where his mind is fogged and forgets about what he should be concentrating on, being an Assassin.
AC III is short on espionage and heavy on combat. (oh wow, an AC game short on espionage and heavy on combat, go figure) But the combat is amazing and actually improves from the previous installments once you get used to the controls.
You get to meet a lot of historical figures, and while I enjoyed their presence, they clutter the game and it seems like the writers tried to juggle around the historical figures without making any of them close acquaintances, aside from the fictional Achilles Davenport. I would have liked to see more of the Culper Spy ring, as they would have been a huge bonuse in terms of espionage, but Ubisoft looked the other way with their revenge mission.
The graphics are great. I feel like I shouldn't have to mention that. This is Ubisoft after-all. And they didn't lie when they said the frontier was huge. I mean, it's huge, bigger than Rome. And then you also get Boston and New York City. I'm glad they added the two cities as runnig around the frontier got old rather quickly. It's just too big with too little content, as in story. There are citizen missions and hunting and frontiersman. Okay, there's actually a lot to do in the frontier, it's just a real pain getting around.
Did I mention all the content in the game? Building the homestead, recruiting assassins, saving citizens, naval missions, collecting trinkets, collecting feathers, finding treasures, capturing forts held by the templars/British, frontiersman missions, hunting missions, Boston brawlers, getting convoys, getting the almanac pages. There's a lot of content, including the DLC, which I found fantastic. (Mainly The Tyranny of Washington, and the Benedict Arnold DLC)
Well, while the story wasn't the high point, the setting, the side missions, the naval missions and a bunch of other stuff really made up for it.

In many ways Assassin's Creed 3 is a confused game torn between what works and what doesn't. On one hand you have Assassin's Creed's now already signature phenomenal world realization in every respect, which happens to sadly be offset by being in a game which simply can't get me to give a damn in the grand scheme things. This off-putting switch in question occurs after a sizable prologue section when game replaces a much more charismatic stand-in main character with a proper one who has all the likeability of a lonesome rock. And that's probably the main fault of AC3 - Connor simply cannot carry the weight to be an interesting character and, by proxy, make for an interesting game. This results in clearly emotional moments and twists falling flat on their faces because there's ZERO emotional investment going on. Your mileage will also obviously vary depending on how much you're into the time period in question, but this has always been one of the stipulations for the series.
That's not to say Connor's personality backed by bad-to-forgettable VA is the only thing at fault here, though. Replacing sprawling cities of previous games with trailblazing colonial towns and explorable frontier was honestly because it directly cuts into the effective use of series' hallmark parkouring abilities. But once again, this is seemingly balanced out with the inclusion of brand new sailing segments which manage to, for the most part, be optional and not overstay their welcome... unlike the all-present repetition seen in other activities throughout the game. Last thing that boggles the mind: why change the control scheme, but still retain the need to keep the run button pressed at all times leading to chronic case of Death Grip?

What can i say about this game? That it's a dissapointment. But let's take it point by point.
Firstly, what i always liked best about the game, the world. In this game it's not very enjoyable. It does look very detailed and realistic, but the movement fluidity suffers greatly for it. The frointeir is the best example of what is wrong with this part of the game; it's large, nice to look at, but almost completelly devoid of stuff to do. There is also no practical way to fast travel though it, which means that no matter how good-looking the forests might be, the game will foce you to run though them so much, that you'll wish the environment was destructivle, just so that you could vent your frustration.
Secondly, combat. This is actually the best aspect of the game. The attacks and counters are not guaranteed, you'll need to focus on them, which makes them more satisfying. The game furnishes you with a lot of melee weapons, so you can pick your favourite style. Not against animals though, there you need to qte or die. The problem with melee combat is that more than a half of it is never explained and not obvious, and yet required by missions.
There is also ranged combat, well, this is nice. But it's inefficient and pointless, really. You'll try it for a bit and go back to swords and daggers.
Lastly there are additional gadgets like rope darts, which give you additional kill mechanisms like hanging your opponent. This is nice sometimes, but again is largely pointless and will be disregarded by most players.
Now then, the missions. These are nice in the beginning, but boring later. The synchronization is either not challenging, or frustrating due to poor design, depending on mission. The ship missions are badass though, but again suffer from synch failures.
The worst aspect of the game are the characters. Connor is ♥♥♥♥♥ty and annoying. He is also painfully bland, which he tries to make up for by yelling, a lot. Think an annoying cousin of bruce willis here. The other characters are even worse. The story characters are just sad to talk about. The british ones are caricatures, clearly the game devs thought that making this a yankee doodle with bad, evil british would sell well in the US, sad just sad.
The last good part of the game is the multiplayer, which is still good and adds some new modes.
Some last thoughts. The crafting system is long winded and pointless. The minigames are horrible as the AI never makes a mistake. The historical reality is an insult. Lastly, side missions and activities are ENTIRELY POINTLESS, like much of the rest of this game.
I recommend that you stay away from the game. Some other reviews will point out some singular good points in the game, but all in all it's a huge mess, which will never be fixed as Ubisoft doesn't give a toss about old games.

There are a few problems with this game here and there. I'll outline them first before getting on with the review.
First: It's not the greatest in terms of stability. For my copy, it shut down exactly every fifteen minutes until I looked up the Community Guide written by user Shizuku on how to fix most of the problems. My issue was solved when I disabled the Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Service. Such a weird thing.
Second: This game's really only for the fans. The Story Mode is a barely there collection of missions without more than a paragraph of explanation as to what's going on in the story. It's kind of like going through Arcade mode on a pure fighting game with a tiny bit more backstory to each fight. It also skips over several major events, such as the Zabuza arc or pretty much everything that's not coming from Naruto's point of view. Really, the Story Mode only acts as Achievement fuel and a barrier to unlocking every character for Versus Mode.
Third: Speaking of Achievements, four of them are broken. Finish with a Tool, finishing a Downed Opponent with a kick, finishing with a Support Ninjutsu, and finishing with a Support Combo only count for Steam if you do them in Free Battle mode.
Fourth, and finally: The game's too short. I played it for fourteen hours and finished it. Every mission, every unlockable. I feel like if we'd gotten more story context, side-arcs (Seriously, Sasuke and Sakura barely factor into this game until the last few missions), and other things that have shown up in future Ultimate Ninja Storm games, it would've added some padding to make this seem more acceptable. As-is, I'd only pick it up if it were on sale. But I'm also not playing it just for the fighting and I have no local friends to do versus mode with.
Now, I'd still recommend this for play. The story may be weak, but the missions and minigames are still generally fun to go through. The game is fairly easy, except for the fights with Kimimaro near the end. While the rest of the game was easy-to-challenging, Kimimaro was downright punishing. I don't really consider this a flaw, though, since he's an end-game character. In comparison, the final boss, Sasuke, is almost a letdown compared to Kimimaro.
The graphics are pretty great, the characters all move and fight like they do on the show, and the Ultimates are very satisfying to watch once you've landed one. Even though the controls are pretty simple and near identical, each character comes off as unique simply because of how your commands are executed, and there are small touches like how some characters can combo shuriken for 20+ hits, some simply throw explosives, and some throw either a gigantic shuriken or a trio and call it a day.
I will take a moment to say how I wish some things had been explained better. The benefits of Awakenings aren't immediately obvious (and, in some cases, remain a total mystery. Naruto's Awakening changes his gameplay entirely, but I've got no clue what Shikamaru or Tenten's modes do.), I think I missed a tutorial on how to unlock Storm Mode and had to figure it out on my own, and Jutsu Clashes were a total surprise to me when I finally pulled one off. It took me a while to get the hang of Substitutions, but once I stopped buttonmashing and started timing my opponent's combos, it really made those a lot simpler.
That said, if you can get the game for cheaper than $20, like in the Trilogy or Legacy bundles, go ahead and do it. It's short, but fun. Just don't go in expecting to understand what's going on if you're new to the series. Street Fighter's had more in-depth Story Modes.

As a little kid, the Road Rash games made we want to travel...and maybe bash people with chains a bit, but I loved the sense of freedom and power. Road Redemption does a million things better than those games from two decades ago, but also has yet to unlock that sense of agency and independence.
What has me writing my review today is that the project has been receiving a lot of attention from its developer over the past several weeks with a constant stream of updates that add content and improve gameplay. The developer is clearly putting a lot of heart into making this a classic, and I want to add my voice in getting it the attention it deserves.
The Good:
Bonkers races that just don't appear in other racing games
Modern graphics
Attacks include kicks, grabs, firearms, timebombs, and a slew of melee weapons from makeshift to medieval
RPG character unlocks & between-race buff shop
Bathooks
Gamepad support
The Bad:
Almost no control over races or progression
You pick your bike at the start of a game and you ride it until you die
Autos' behavior is almost always erratic and sometimes inexplicable (driving off bridges, into cliffs, etc.)
Crazy races, an array of weapons, gamepad support and constantly improving gameplay make this a title I keep coming back to play rather than just wait for it to all be finished.

Fez is a cute little package of platforming, puzzles, and a wonderfully creative 3D system that allows you to traverse 3D worlds one 2D plane at a time.
What you need to know here is that the crux of this game is the 2D/3D system.  It is well done, it adds to both the platforming and puzzle elements.
The platforming can be best described as platforming light.  There are very few parts that offer a meaningful challenge, but that is okay.  The puzzles like wise are not essential but can range from quite tough to impossible, yet are so tangential that it won't ruin your expereince if you can't complete them.
If you have some free time to kill get Fez.  It might not be so engrossing that it should be labeled a must play, but Fez is an endearing game and well worth your time.

This game is basically a puzzle platformer that requires almost no platforming skills. In fact there is only one room (rising lava *cough*) that was remotely challenging for a non expert like me. The focus of this game lies on exploration. The world is beautifully crafted and contains puzzles that were too hard for me to figure out on my own. It has been a long time since I had to consult the internet that often for hints.
That being said: If you like hard puzzles and exploration, this is the game for you. This game uses it's own alphabet and number system and you have to learn both of them before you can even grasp most of the puzzles. Oh and you should definitely play with a controller because some puzzles actually use the vibrations to tell you what to do.

FEZ is a game about platforming, solving puzzles and finding cubes as you explore a relaxing and beautiful 2D world. What makes this platformer different is the fact that it's only semi-2D, as you can change the perspective. Every level is actually 4 2D levels that are mashed together into a single 3D level.
The platforming in this game isn't special, but the puzzles are. As you can see by my play time, I was one of those people who used guides to get 100%, but I really regret it. If I could time travel, I would go back in time, punch myself in the face and tell myself to actually do the puzzles. If you aren't a lazy sh*t like me, you can actually spend time writing things down, solving ciphers, looking for clues, scanning IQ codes and so on, so forth. There are so many amazing puzzles in this game that you can triple the game time just by spending some time thinking.
The graphics really add to the experience. The game is very chill and some beautiful backdrops make this one of the most relaxing games that I have played. The music was also great, an overall, I found myself really enjoying this game. If you're a fellow completionist, there are even more reasons as to why should you get the game - the game doesn't have any "bake 10000000 pies" or "finish the game in 10 minutes" achievements. All you gotta do is run around, find collectibles and use a guide, cause, even though you can be better than me, let's face it, you won't find all 3 red cubes without a guide.
I don't think this is a work of genius but I definitely enjoyed this and I recommend this to absolutely everyone.

However, my main problems with this game is how unfair it feels the further you progress in the game. Most enemies are cannon fodder and die very quickly to your laser guns. But whenever you have to fly a ground mission, which is almost 2/3rd of the game, you *will* encounter droid tanks. And for some inexplicable reason, those tanks are perfect at destroying land *and* air units. The sheer amount of tanks and the amount of damage they can do to you is absolutely unbalanced, but whenever you get hit, the screen shakes and you will miss your current target. Apart from this, the final mission, which I won't spoil, is emblematic for the obfuscated mission goals the game throws at you. You never really know where you *should* go, you *can* go pretty much anywhere, but you might get ambushed by sudden enemy spawns right in front of you. When I started the game, I thought it was fun but the more I progressed, the less fun and more frustrating it became. Don't buy this at full price, it isn't worth it.

People did not like The Phantom Menace much, so this game was already at a disadvantage as it came out.
Combine that with clunky controls that are hard to set up to work halfway intuitively. My play sessions consisted of a single mission, maybe two, at a time and every time I started up the game I rebound the keys ever so slightly to make them slightly better for me.
By the time the final mission rolled around I was finally pleased with how it felt, and the game was entirely enjoyable.
The plot isn't anything special, but it's sufficiently seeped in Star Wars lore that it was entertaining for me. It features a cast of three new characters experiencing the invasion of Naboo and getting caught up in the conflict. Missions are split up about 50/50 between planetary battles and space battles, but you are always in one of the three titular Starfighters. Each character has his/her own ship, which controls slightly differently and has different secondary weapons and looks.
It's not the huge budget movie tie-in you might be used to, but those also tend to be very bad.
If you're patient enough to jump in and out to tweak the controls to work for you and have some fondness for Star Wars that at least somewhat extends to the prequel trilogy this might be a fun title to pick up.

I have been a huge fan of the AC series and have legitimately enjoyed every single game except for the Chronicle games. I have been known to be leniant toward the series about things that a lot of other people are usually much harsher about. Here's why I am absolutely loving AC Origins so far. It is completely and 100% seamless, where the only loading screens (that are pretty short on a HDD btw) are when you fast travel and going in and coming out of cutscenes. Unlike in the previous games where there's a loading screen anytime you leave a city and such, this game has none of that. The size of the world and the seamlessness reminds me of the Witcher 3's world. The controls are a bit confusing at first because they changed it from the previous games so veterans of the series might be put off at first HOWEVER there is an alternate control scheme that is basically classic AC controls. The modern era stuff, which a lot of people dislike, is very minor like in AC Unity and Syndicate. Hunting and wildlife is a lot more immersive and well done compared to AC 3 and Black Flag. There is microtransactions in the game HOWEVER they are actually completely unnecessary and a nonfactor in the game, you can get any outfit, money, etc. all on your own in the game at a reasonable pace. MT's are there, but please do not let that deter you, because you definitely don't need them. This also seems to be one of the best optimized games in the series as well. I have a 1080Ti and an Intel i7 Quad Core and at max settings I get straight 60 FPS. Your mileage may vary obviously if you have a weaker system but from first glance and the amount of possible graphics options available in the settings, it is very much optimised well, way better than Unity, Syndicate, and even Black Flag. Also, for those who care about Steam achievements, its also the first AC game to have Steam achievements which is nice.
If I had one complaint about the game so far, is that like previous games, in the beginning parts of the world are block by story progression. It doesn't last long, but its there. If I were to give it an arbitrary score out of 10, it'd be 9/10.
EDIT: I forgot to mention, but another major plus is that they have gotten rid of optional objectives, allowing for much more freedom with missions and much less frustrations. However they have also gotten rid of the memory sequence system, where you could replay missions and the like.
EDIT #2: Do not sit on this game. It really is THE best in the series and that's from someone who already loves the series.

Initial Review, Will post another one at a later date
Coming from the "Diablo" world, I've had a hard time finding an MMO I really could just "dive in" and enjoy. TERA REALLY caught me off guard, being free and all. So far, the combat system is SO much better and more "Diablo" style than ANY other MMO (I've tried - WoW, Neverwinter, GW1/2, Rift, SWKOTR, etc[all the big ones essentially]).
My BIGGEST complaint with MMO's is the countless hours you spend "figuring it out". No, the games aren't especially difficult, but to get the most out of the game, you have to spend a huge chunk of time just figuring out where to go, much less what to do when you get there. This game is super intuitive, and its very very easy to figure out what you're supposed to be doing.
PROS -
- game looks ridiculously good!
- intuitive operation, seamless "point and click" navigation
- super helpful "help" menu (shocking!)
- combat is engaging and youre "in the fight". None of that *click-lock* crap from the other MMO's. You aim AND you can actively dodge/block! Its so much fun!
- generous drops; so far (level 25) this game has not felt "pay to win", "pay to get ahead" or any of that other shenanigans going on. They want you to buy the "elite" package, but thats ok. I will be upgrading most likely. Item progression is extremely fair and balanced (So far....)
- I don't feel like I'm "grinding" (wow players know what Im talking about!). Im taking some time to level up, explore, and general get to know the game, but I am getting a healthy amount of exp in the interim. I've seen some complaints of the "grind" starting at level 10 or so, but that's truely not the case.
- I started with the berserker, so I have been able to solo without any problems at all. Apparently some classes are incapable of soloing -> PLAY WITH A FRIEND!
- in store purchases seem fairly generous compared to other games. 10$ for a high end, unique mount? Pretty cool.
- MAPS ARE HUGE!!!!!
- item progression has been awesome. In the "other" mmo's, i find myself stuck with the same basic armor for many levels. Level 22? Still running with a level 6 greaves on? Malarky! This game rewards you with loot, and it only gets better.
CONS
- game is pretty taxing on a computer. I run an i7-4790k with an r9 290x, and Im on "medium" settings (nuts!)
- VERY sexualized. As a heterosexual man, I enjoy boobs and butts as much as the next guy, but holy crap! It would be ok if it was merely an "option" but there have been no "tank" looking female characters in the game I've seen so far, and as my armor progresses, I get more and more scantily clad lol.  Luckily, its just a side product of whats going on.
- MAPS ARE HUGE!!!!!!! (Ok. My issue is going back and forth between some quests can literally take 20 minutes if you dont have a teleport scroll. Thats a bit "much" imo)
- randomized loot can really bite you in the butt.
Things that would make this game perfect ->
1) optionalize the gratuitous sexualization (yeah yeah... haha)
2) make random loot drops more "fair". I.e. if one player gets a higher end item, and you've been getting crap, tilt the drop rate to your favor, and lower that players.
3) make teleport scrolls a vendor item (is it? I've not come across any minus drops from monsters)

So you're in charge of a wagon train/space ship/whatever full of colonistcicles, flying to a new planet and banging your head against popup encounters, making decisions that invariably kill your crew, damage your ship and take away all your money.
So why is Quantum flux so bad when Oregon Trail wasn't?
* It doesn't have any particularly interesting gameplay over Oregon Trail
* The artwork is so low effort it's painful - fonts are mismatched, art assets are bad for the 1990s
* Technical low effort junk - It's clearly a tablet/mobile port, and what's absurd - you can't even switch to fullscreen.  Windowed mode only!
The laziness and low quality in this game is painful.  You can play OT online for free.  There are better web browser games.  The developer has no justification to put this on the Steam store and ask for money for it.

I'm torn about whether to recommend this game or not. If we had a rating scale, I would give it a 3/5. Let me explain.
Quantum Flux, at first glance, is a space adventure inspired by games like FTL, and perhaps even The Oregon Trail. It's fun, each time you jump, not knowing what you will find. This is fun, and I find myself excited when the ship launches into a new area.
However, after playing a couple of times, you quickly notice that although each jump leads you to a semi-random encounter, the scenario and results of each encounter are always the same. It becomes a memory game rather than a risky adventure.
Additionally, in the few games I played, the game usually leans towards the positive, so if you choose the option that sounds like the nicest guy would choose, you will get the best results. I kept hoping that this would sometimes backfire, but it was always the same.
Then on my third play, I encountered a bug(?) which is why I will now be uninstalling the game. The whole premise is that you are taking the last of humanity to Haven. Well, I managed to get the ship back into known space, and my crew told me we could now jump straight to Haven. After the conversation, the ship auto-jumped, and I expected an end game screen before credits rolled... but instead I got another random encounter, and at the end of that encounter, it was mentioned that I still had a long way to go. So apparently, it's not possible to actually complete the game.
I should also mention that you cannot adjust the resolution, and it plays in either a tiny window, or a pixelated full screen mode.
Therefore, although there is fun to be had here, and a puzzle to solve in figuring out the best approach to every encounter, the game is in need of some improvements before I could recomend it. If you get it cheap in a bundle, give it a try, otherwise I recommend giving FTL another play instead.

Okay, memes aside, I recently bought this on steam, but have previously put MANY hours in on xbox since its release, and almost 5 years later it has remained one of my favorite games to date. Fez is a 2.5D puzzle-platformer where you shift the perspective of your world to line up platforms in clever ways to progress and collect golden cubes. And thats all there is to it... except its so much more than that.
First and foremost, the platforming is incredibly smooth and intuitive, and they've managed to give a tiny little 2D character a real sense of weight. The art and graphics are stylistically beautiful, and complemented by an absolutely incredible soundtrack by the man himself Disasterpeace, it perfectly captures the derelict and dreamlike essence of the world you're in. As you progress, you encounter many different realms and ruins to traverse and explore, and slowly uncover the faint but intriguing lore about your past through mysterious runes and drawings. Past the initial objective of collecting cubes, you begin to encounter anti-cubes, intoducing the brilliantly cryptic puzzle aspect of the game and creating a parallel to the main casual gameplay experience.
While some would argue that, aside from its perspective-shifting mechanic, the platforming adds not much new in gameplay, I find it to be loads of fun, and it's the sheer atmosphere and imaginative detail that really sell it for me. I recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone who wants a challenging, immersive, nostalgic experience with beautiful retro-esque art, incredible music, and fantastic atmosphere.

Fez is an amazing puzzle game. It's uses many cool plays on perspective throughout the game, which itself consists entirely of non-stop puzzles, both platforming and thinking out of the box types, and I loved them all. There is a New Game+ option too for even tougher puzzles, and some lategame crazy difficult/obscure puzzles that I had to look online for help with. All in all, 10/10 love the game.

Let me start off by saying that I thought this game was good. Despite that, I don't think I enjoyed the game to its fullest extent. I thought it was fun and despite being a pixel based game (not that there's anything wrong with that), it felt really fleshed out. In particular, I really enjoyed being able to change the views of whatever level you were currently in, it made it seem large and 3D despite mainly being 2D based.
It may sound strange, but to me, the way this game's story/universe is treated reminds me of Dark Souls. You're thrown in and whatever you learn about this world is based on your own interpretations of what you see/experience for yourself. With this game, it was a little bit more abstract. Most of what's revealed about this game's setting/universe is based off of pictures, the musings of your mostly inactive "partner", and the various types of levels that you go through. Honestly, I didn't really like how it was done in this game. I'm sure the game's universe is fully fleshed out, but trying to decipher what's going on just from pictures/your surroundings just isn't for me. I enjoy how it's done in Dark Souls because at least it's partially explained, but in this game there's no real explanation. Maybe it's because I didn't 100% this game, but based off of what I played, that's how I feel about it.
In general, Fez is a 2D/3D platformer that can also be viewed as a puzzle game. For the most part, it's interesting trying to find the cube bits in every level, but as the game goes on it can be frustrating. Despite the game having a map to try and make navigation easier for you, I still found it difficult. Most of the travelling in this game is done through doors and warp gates found in various levels. The warp gates and doors were easy to use for short distance travel, but for some reason I found it difficult to use when I wanted to travel long distances. I had to frequently check the map to see that I was going in the right place, but some levels had so many doors that I had to guess and check which one would be the one to lead me to where I wanted to go. Maybe I'm stupid, but it just didn't feel as organized as it could've been.
Overall, I enjoyed the game, but as i previously stated, I didn't fully enjoy what it had to offer. This is the type of game that's for gamers that like to fully immerse themselves inside of a game's world and like to figure things out for themselves. I enjoy both of those things, but something about this game just felt off for me.
Based on what I enjoyed about this game, I give it a 3.5/5. I could easily see people giving this game a 4 or even a 4.5/5, but some things just prevented me from fully enjoying the game. I recommend this game if you enjoy 2D/3D platformers and games with a blurred narrative.
If you're searching for a game that you'll never forget playing and fall in love with, then look no further.

My problems with the game were mainly the grinding that got boring and was the majorty of  what you do in the game play , and the literally "forced" plot. Why is forced plot a problem? In theory it's quite good. But when you calculate the exact amount of money and time you want to spend in a place before you go to your house to sleep/eat and insted get transported around the city with *no way* of skipping the dialog or speeding up the text(which just got really annoying the more I played).
A way to solve it is to let the player choose when to enter the sequance. For example, when you get that wierd suitcase to your house instead of forcing you to start it's event just let me do it whenever I please.
Another problem for me was the fact that you can't tell the difficulity of a fight pre-entring it. There is no indication of what level the fight/quest you're going into requires and once you start a quest you can't quit/stop it.
For me it got really annoying when the pizza guy gave me a job (special delivery) and when I got to it the fight was unwinable for my level.
And in a game where time investment matters, and thinking ahead about what to do really matters (you can get injured and thus slow your progress for example)  this kind of problems shine and are really, really annoying.
And ofcourse the last and really major problem of this game for me was the money vs. training problem. It really feels unbalanced so that inorder to gain just a little bit of money you need to spend an entire day and then you need to rest in bed, lift your spirit and eat alot(food seems really expansive compared to the money you get). In other words, the "day" in the game is way too short to get money to survive ,recuperate , and train. and most times even two days are no enough which is ridiculous in terms of in-game managment.
If all of those things were to be fixed/balanced I'd give the game another chance.

Let me start off by saying that I thought this game was good. Despite that, I don't think I enjoyed the game to its fullest extent. I thought it was fun and despite being a pixel based game (not that there's anything wrong with that), it felt really fleshed out. In particular, I really enjoyed being able to change the views of whatever level you were currently in, it made it seem large and 3D despite mainly being 2D based.
It may sound strange, but to me, the way this game's story/universe is treated reminds me of Dark Souls. You're thrown in and whatever you learn about this world is based on your own interpretations of what you see/experience for yourself. With this game, it was a little bit more abstract. Most of what's revealed about this game's setting/universe is based off of pictures, the musings of your mostly inactive "partner", and the various types of levels that you go through. Honestly, I didn't really like how it was done in this game. I'm sure the game's universe is fully fleshed out, but trying to decipher what's going on just from pictures/your surroundings just isn't for me. I enjoy how it's done in Dark Souls because at least it's partially explained, but in this game there's no real explanation. Maybe it's because I didn't 100% this game, but based off of what I played, that's how I feel about it.
In general, Fez is a 2D/3D platformer that can also be viewed as a puzzle game. For the most part, it's interesting trying to find the cube bits in every level, but as the game goes on it can be frustrating. Despite the game having a map to try and make navigation easier for you, I still found it difficult. Most of the travelling in this game is done through doors and warp gates found in various levels. The warp gates and doors were easy to use for short distance travel, but for some reason I found it difficult to use when I wanted to travel long distances. I had to frequently check the map to see that I was going in the right place, but some levels had so many doors that I had to guess and check which one would be the one to lead me to where I wanted to go. Maybe I'm stupid, but it just didn't feel as organized as it could've been.
Overall, I enjoyed the game, but as i previously stated, I didn't fully enjoy what it had to offer. This is the type of game that's for gamers that like to fully immerse themselves inside of a game's world and like to figure things out for themselves. I enjoy both of those things, but something about this game just felt off for me.
Based on what I enjoyed about this game, I give it a 3.5/5. I could easily see people giving this game a 4 or even a 4.5/5, but some things just prevented me from fully enjoying the game. I recommend this game if you enjoy 2D/3D platformers and games with a blurred narrative.

Fez is an amazing platformer/puzzler centered around the unique ability to shift between four 3-dimensional planes within a 2-dimensional space. The game follows Gomez on his quest to restore order to his shattered world.
Fez is one of the few games I have 100% completion on for a reason. The dimension-shifting ability is just so fun and interesting to play with, I was never bored even when stuck on a particular puzzle. It's been a long time since I've played a game that made it so compelling to actually collect all of the collectibles.
The other standout feature of Fez is its art. The pixel-graphics are gorgeously detailed and the world was meticulously crafted so each realm you visited would feel like it belonged.
I whole-heartedly recommend you checking out Fez as it truly is one of the greatest platformer/puzzlers I've ever had the experience of playing.

If you want to fly around in a starfighter in the Star Wars universe, then this game should be fun for you. This game provides a different view of the Naboo invasion than what's shown in the movies, which makes the story somewhat interesting.
Normally I don't like flight simulations, but I enjoyed this game... when I wasn't being blown up by missiles or tanks. In the missions where you face swarms of enemy fighters (the last mission in particular) you become immersed in the dog-fighting. Also, the graphics aren't horrible either.
The controls do take a little getting used too, particularly turning/rolling (which uses E and R while A and D switch targets). Once you get the hang of things the game is fun.... until it suddenly ends. The game is short (took me <5 hours on medium) but it's an enjoyable ride nonetheless.
One other negative aspect is the final boss who is a pain with his missiles which go through your shields and his health restarts after each of the first 2 sections of the boss fight. Also, there is a lack of direction of where to go for the fight. I lost the boss in the middle of it and was flying around in a hangar area for a few minutes before seeing a passageway to go through. The boss is tough, even on easy. This boss just seems out of place with the difficulty of the rest of the game.
Overall, this game is good for a few hours of fun and definitely worth the money if you see it on sale. Also, the game is good for making you dizzy and to lose your sense of up and down. All this is achieved by spaceships that seem to be able to halt and turn in an instant with no regard to speed and inertia.

I got beef about some stuff, while loving others. check it all to make sense of the chaos of this review.
I ended up referencing a few other titles while doing this, whether that is a no no or not.. I guess we'll see.
+It looks looks wondrous.
+Ran smooth so far ( FX 6300 3.5ghz & GTX 970 ssc, high settings or above)
+Gentle on my GPU. Something like SoW makes my card really run its fans, 65% or higher, to the point I can almost hear it through my headphones. This doesn't do it. Not by much, and I appreciate that.
+The map so far is well designed, very lush and lively. I've enjoyed exploring it so far.
+The RPGness of it. Skills to acquire, gear to craft, all the weapons and equipment. But that's a double edged sword to get to later.
+
No but really, it's nice to have a new one release. The story telling so far has been pretty good and I look forward to doing more.
+Side Quests so far all have dialog. It's a very Witcher styled feeling beyond that though. To really be prepared for story quests, side ones are strongly recommended.
+
It feels so good. It really does feel so good to walk the city. So much focus about Egypt, and you forget what all you were gonna actually run into here. It's been minorly breathtaking.
+Soundtrack is pleasant. Same person who worked on Ac4 and Unity did this. I really enjoyed Black Flag, and parts of Unity's sound track, so it I'm diggin it.
+Depth. The year off I think gave Ubi the time they needed to ensure everyone felt more alive. Bayek is a fun character to watch develope more. And Aya isn't just a ghost. She has depth too, not such a fling as Elise. And they're oh so lovely together it mades me feel lonely.
+Plenty of cutscenes, voices, and excellent writing for small moment that give you giggles and nods.
+Reality has a third person thing again. I know some hate it for not simply being Desmond, but I like it so far.
+Easter Eggs hinting as franchises in the same universe are pretty cool.
-Its RPGness. It adds a new depth to the game you otherwise never had, but it brings in flaws. It reminds me of Division. In this, a headshot with an arrow can not always kill.
I do not like that entirely. It's two small details about the whole style, but they're big deals to me.
-Stealth (assassinating) is underwhelming. I've since upgraded a lot of tools, learned the methods, and know how to creep far better, but it still lacks. They put forth so much effort into the combat, they left the stealth lack luster in return it feels. It's still better than any other in terms of creep stealthing though really. I'd enjoy seeing something like Blacklist method and variety for silent murder in future titles with Bayek. Can really only chalk it up now as Bayek isn't really an Assassin in this one. He's a Warrior, a Guardian. Doesn't have the finesse for it yet. It's why his attacks are only one of a handful. No fancy takedowns. One can hope for the future though for more fluidity.
-Social stealth is absent. No more blending. You hide in bushes, or out of line of sight, but no more. I realize there is a franchise long debate about how it should or shouldn't work. Some tasks now, I kinda wish I could still do so. Being in Alexandria and not being able to upsets me.
-/+Combat. I put this as a mix because it isn't outright
You lose situational awareness the rest gave you before, though enough time has alleviated that. It's For Honor, thrusted into AC. It's how I've come to see it so far. Instead of the whole area being seen and having the scope of the whole fight available, it tunnel visions it to your front. That works in FH, seeing how the game was designed with the 1v1 encounters in mind. In this? It's a bit more detrimental to your health. I died a few times consecutively because I'm fighting average guys, and big Brutus here comes barreling from off screen and sticks a club in a place it shouldn't be. The locking system was weird, but eventually got used to it too. A soft version of Dark Souls maybe. Lock, block and strafe. Or don't at all, you don't have to after all.
There's a learning curve. For combat, and stealth. It gets easier. The skills, which I really should have mentioned somewhere, do each improve your gameplay. So it's helpful to pick and choose based on what you want to strengthen, or balance out your weaknesses.
-
At first I had complaints you couldn't drop down right, couldn't decent safely and the such. I've since learned the proper method. A for controller, literally does it all for you. to close gaps up or down, jump straight forward, etc. B to decent is more for dropping to ledges. And you can still roll to avoid damage, you just need to tap A on landing. (A lack of high profile though I believe also limits the stealth capabilities.)
-I can't f&$%ing sprint mang? Dude can move at a healthy pace, but there is no, "Okay, go, NOW." speed. It's annoying. Camels are neat. Horses are nicer. All I need now is a suped up ricer. (Why did I rhyme that?)
-Random audio buzzing in various moment. It's just.. what? As I update this, I get them more and more often. Just a solid second of
and then the game goes on. Happens in cutscene transitions, or after deaths.
-Equipment screen is interesting. Two bows, two melee weapons, and one active tool. So to change dart types or bombs, you need to go into the menu itself and change. Weapons swapping between two isn't bad, but given current strength, I find myself needing to swap out empty bows for other two which are full often. Each bow type has its own ammo type as well, which I guess is nice.
As you level up, you get more power obviously. Bows work better, and having quiver upgrades stretch out time. Ensuring you loot prolongs a bow's use too.
-
I realize I said no sprinting earlier, but a revisit to dying from lack of speed to escape brings me back here. I know making games isn't easy, but we need something that Ac3 had with horses. Come on Ubi.
It's fun. Not the same AC. It has For Honor, Witcher and Far Cry vibes. Even a little hint of Wildlands, eagle being the drone, minus exploding. Was also suggested it's a tad bit of Zelda. I never played them though, so I cannot say for certain.
If you don't mind it being a different feel, then for sure get it. If you cling to older AC styles too much, didn't like For Honor or Witcher that much, maybe watching a stream is a better choice, until maybe a sale or something.
However! Don't let me entirely deter you! I am enjoying myself, despite the distinct changes. It's a fresh breathe of air otherwise. Truth be told, AC hasn't really been the same since a blended line of Revelations and 3 anyway. Give it a chance if you want it. I
recommend it after all. The more I play it, the more it does feel like AC. I missed this.

I wanted not to like this game, I really wanted it. But I have been disapointed, I love it.
There is two things I hate in other games, which are indeed in Fez too : excessive backtracking, and puzzles where you need to write down everything in order to just understand them.
But
The backtracking is ok, since you unlock several portals. And since the world is huge. And beautiful. And alive. The world is alive, lots of way-too-much cute animals jumping and flying and doing whatever cuties are doing. So, in the end the backtrack thing is not a big problem since it's a pleasure to travel through this world.
As I said earlier, the world is huge. Several times I entered a zone thinking I will find one or two rooms, and ending finding tones of new secrets, new paths, or ten-ish new rooms. Even if those rooms are almost empty, you may enjoy just the adventure and exploration.
The mechanics are great, and really well-used for the platforms part of the game, sometimes even for the puzzle. The jump is a bit weird though, with some kind of momentum but you'll get used to it easily.
Yes, this game is a puzzle-plateformer-exploration-retro-game, and doing great in every of those styles.
The game isn't easy, I can't say it's hard because, as I said, I "cheated", but I guess if you're trying to 100% it (rushing the end isn't hard at all), be sure you can play for long hours and be patient.

Gomez encounters a strange cube that gives him a fez.  Gomez wakes up in the world he just woke up in, except the world he once knew as flat now has dimensions to navigate in search of cubes to unlock doors and move to the next level.  Gomez must do all this to save the world from destroying itself.  Use your map often, spin the world around, and see where each next jump brings you.

Fez is a puzzle platformer, but honestly it's about 20 times more puzzle than platformer.
You start off in a small village, as a ... thingy ... called Gomez. Soon, a mysterious old man shows you to this astral ... place ... and you get a fez. With the fez, you can switch the perspective, and as little Gomez is testing it out, something goes terribly wrong, and the game crashes. It starts off again, but you can see purposely placed bugs, and Gomez is wearing the fez. You are told that you have just bassically started the end of the universe, and only you can stop it, by finding all 32 golden cubes. The actual game starts, and I rather liked the perspective changes. It added a nice new layer to the puzzle, and I sometimes forgot that you could change perspective, and ended up stuck for 30 minutes, finally realising that the answere was within a push of a button. After 15 minutes you come to a crossroad, except that there's literally 20 different routes you could go. You don't go to different places in a specific order, you kind of just discover them. In fact, I was extremely overwhelmed by the number of decisions, but I just decided to fully complete each area before I moved on to the next. There are not only golden cubes, but also anti cubes, and they are harder to get, often in complex puzzles. The game kind of creates it's own code, with different symbols, telling you to do a certain combo move. You don't need any anti cubes to finish the game, but if you have all golden and anti cubes, you get a little surprise...
There are also the 3 red cubes, which require extreme thinking to work out, but luckily you don't need them.
Overall this game is good and ymanaged to 100% complete it ( except for the red cubes) so get it if you like puzzles and exploring ima give it 8/10 stars yay

First pros and cons then my personal thoughts.
Pros:
+Good story.
+Intresting characters.
+Conversations between characters are worth listing to.
+Driving greatly improved.(and thats playing with keyboard and mouse)
+Intresting protaganist.
+Hacking has been expanded and fleshed out.
+Good graphics.
+Parkour is fun.
+Animatons are smooth.
+Fun seemless multiplayer.(fun with a friend, but can be dull playing alone)
+Side quests aren't repetitive and each one is different.
+Light hearted/funny.
+Characters don't feel dull and lifeless.
+GRAPHICS HAVEN'T BEEN DOWNGRADED.
+World feels alive.
+Lots of cutizimation.(clothes only, guns and gadgets cars are limited)
+Good optizimation.(running on a gtx 1050ti and a i7 2600k, 8gbs of ram)
+Has lots of internet jokes.(memes)
Cons:
-Game will crash sometimes for doing nothing.
-Shooting can feel slow and clunky.(but acceptable)
-For some Users game can have very bad lag spikes when driving and roaming.
-Side activities can feel dull and to easy.(like racing and driver sf)
-When collecting research points or collectibles, etc, some where impossible to get if the player din't have the drone, rc, lifts to get these.(and the lifts where never around when I needed them)
-Tanks are very op and can kill you easly.(ex. lmg can kill you in 3-4 shots and thats rapid fire)
-When detected, all the guards know exactly where you are.
-AI can be smart but dumb at times.
My Thoughts
Coming from Watch Dogs 1 on the xbox 360 is a very big improvement. Watch Dogs 2 improves nearly every ascpect of the first one. No longer you have a cliche story of revenge and a dull, no personality protaganist. Watch Dogs 2 springs to life with memorable characters and funny overblown cutscenes between the characters interacting. The protagainst is longer dull but now a enjoyalbe character who makes jokes and has a very San Franscio personality and full of life. Hacking is no longer limited and has been fleshed out and can have some very halarious results. Driving is now accpetable and handles like aracde racing games. Multiplauer can be fun but dull without a friend. While shooting can be slow and clunky, is still enjoyable. Overall with the good story and characters and combat. I give the game a 8 out of 10. Its just needs to fix some issues with optizmation and shooting ascpects and some of the side content.(refering to racing and drifer sf, which can be dull and way to easy)The game now lays a good framework for future Watch Dogs games look upon and improve on.
Final Score: 8/10

This review comes late, just as late I was in buying it. Having played Watch Dogs and quite hating it, I didn't really thought WD2 could be any better. After trying it out on someone else's box, I found myself really into it, with story and gadgets much more on the hacker/reverse engineer side than the Rambo-commando Forgetful Pierce WD. I played mainly the story mode, and I liked it so much that I decided to stop, buy the game, import the saves and continue from there.
On top of the good campaign and side missions, there are a lot of fun activities, well thought, well varied and small numbered: you will find only 6 races for each type, but this allows a lot of difference and fresh fun, I honestly love it. There are also a lot of other activities, like the
ScoutX, in which you have to picture various locations or people around the city.
This game puts fun ahead of realism, and it's a great thing in my opinion. A lot of other games (à la GTA) really puts the player in often frustrating situations, for the sake of "realism", while WD2 is finely tuned for the fun. A perfect example is a car chase with the cops, sudden turn around, drive into a café, and hide inside the car, and the cops more often than not won't spot you, at least on normal difficulty, have no idea for the higher difficulties.
It has a few bad notes in my book, such as the multiplayer achievements, the hundreds of collectables (as per usual with Ubisoft), but all in all this is the best and well crafted Ubisoft game in quite a while. Definitively better than Watch Dogs, a lot more fun and entertaining, with a world full of lots of non boring, fun, non repetitive activities and gameplay. I highly hope the sequels will follow the same route.
inside Watch Dogs 2 you will find a lot – and I mean it, a lot – of hacking reference (Glider/Game of Life found on t-shirts is a prime example), cracking/reverse engineering references, references and nods to various existing hacking groups and their activities… if you are at least half knowledge on the subject, you can play "spot the reference" on top of the game itself.

Despite its flaws, Hinterland is a fun experience and well worth the ten dollar (non-sale) price tag.
Positives:
+ Good music (what there is) that fits the game's theme well
+ Simple to pick up controls and gameplay
+ Low system requirements
Negatives:
-  Long load times at game startup or resume
- Glitches are common and can be game breaking
- Lackluster presentation and in-game interface
Hinterland is a game that is all about making your own fun. Pick your class and your rules, then begin your journey to conquer the lands around your village, bringing in resources and improving your town's standing as you go.
While the game's overall concept and execution are simple, it is nevertheless an engaging experience. Many other reviewers have likened it to a board game, and that really is the best way to think of it, not as an adventure RPG, but more like a strategy game.
While the game's general performance can be poor, it is never more than a minor nuisance, and the game features a great amount of  replayability.

Original review:
"Unfortunately, the Linux version didn't launch, with no indication as to why. I'm not the only one in this situation - so I don't know if this game is any good! Let's hope the developers can address this soon."
EDIT: alright, update. So I revisited this today and pored over what was going on. So launching it via nw outside of steam gave this gem (amongst a couple of others):
greenworks-linux64.node: undefined symbol: _ZN2v816FunctionTemplate3NewEPNS_7IsolateEPFvRKNS_20FunctionCallbackInfoINS_5ValueEEEENS_5LocalIS4_EENSA_INS_9SignatureEEEi
POW - that's it. To fix this, if you're running on a 64-bit system, simply move the file greenworks-linux64.node out of the way, e.g.
$ cd "~/.local/share/Steam/SteamApps/common/Bloodbath Kavkaz/bin/"
$ mv greenworks-linux64.node greenworks-linux64.node_bak
Now fire it up. Magic! All working, and looks good :)

AC ON THE RIGHT TRACK;
Overall a vast improvement from the past formula. You can tell that Ubisoft did their homework on the setting and added a lot of detail. It feels accurate, the cities and overall world you are in feels alive and lived in. As I played it became apparent they borrowed some stuff from other games like Witcher 3 - with more extensive quest stories- and the way Bayek can investigate for people.
The combat is vastly improved and is made to be more dynamic and quick. You no longer have to go through lenghty non-animus sections, Ubisoft understands that you want to get back into the action, so it never overstays its welcome.
I highly recommend this game, the setting is interesting, the story is better than the past AC entries, the combat is much better, and it rewards exploration with little hand holding. Don't get me wrong, this game isn't perfect, but it is a step in the right direction. So if you like to explore, and immerse yourself completely into one of the most interesting time periods of humanity, you won't regret this purchase.

Great fun, and as everyone else, it's definitely got a lot of Road Rash's gameplay, but it does build upon the base game with a talent tree and such.  I wouldn't say it is worth the full price right now (July 2015, Early Access), but certainly is worth grabbing on sale.  If/when they add in online multiplayer (local-only right now), I think the value will increase.
Compared to many Early Access games, it's fairly polished, but there's a lot that still needs work in the game.
Some of the physics create dumb situations where you can get stuck, even with the jump jets. There's also the oddity of being able to steer while in mid-air - realism vs fun aside, this leads to an easier game than it should be.
The menus are very primitive in appearance, and the UI sound effects could use a lot of work, as they break immersion. It's also non-intuitive to exit the game properly - you can't do it unless you're in a race that's going on, which should be allowed, but shouldn't be the only way!
I'd love to see more progress in being able to buy/unlock new bikes/costumes, even be able to paint things the colors you'd like.

I bought this while on sale for $8.  I would gladly buy again at full price.  Playing local coop with my daugther thirty minutes into the game (almost 10) she was say that this is one of the best games ever.  Not sure about that part yet but it certainly is a fun game and has the makings to be a very good game with further love and development by the developers.  It was certainly even with only an hour spent so far worth the money.   Is it rough around the edges?  Very.  Graphically it isn't anything to write home about.  Sound wise I can't say as we didn't have the sound playing.  I am not much on sound effects anyway so I usually am not big on reviewing that side of games.  I love soundtracks but only when I am playing OST burnt to CDs in my car.  Anyway to me this type of game is all about is it fun.  This isn't a game that is meant to be complex looking so the graphics really aren't that big of deal to me.  They are smooth for the most part so that is what I care about.  There are a few clipping issues that I am sure will get worked out.  Texture wise this isn't meant to be a game you are going to stop and look at the roses anyway.     Control wise I played via keyboard and my daughter via offical 360 controller.  We have a second 360 contoller but I was too lazy to hook up so I am going on her word about the contoller controls but she didn't seem to have any real problems with them.   The keyboard controls using the default WASD/Keyboard controls were fair but had some drift in them.  I am sure the developers will tighten up the controls as game development goes along so I am not too worried about that.   However contol in this type of game is one of the bigger issues worth looking at so if you are wondering as far as July 5th, 2015 at least as far as keyboard controls I can say that the bikes do control a "floaty" that I would like.   Once again this is a EA title and I am sure this will  change.   As far as overall game concept this game follows along with the old Road Rash feel and that is perfect for me.  The game is FUN.  Is it perfect, nope.  Was I expecting it to be at this point, nope.   Do I think it has the chance to become a great game, yes.  At this point in development do I feel like it is worth risking the full asking price of $20?  Yes if you played Road Rash or looking for a fun game that doesn't take itself too serious then I do.   The game doesn't have a lot of "meat" in it yet but even so what is on the bones so far is worth the money.  I have spent a lot more for a lot less fun.
