DO YOU REMEMBER ROAD RASH? DO YOU WANT A MODERN REMAKE OF ROAD RASH? IF YES, BUY THE HELL OUT OF THIS GAME RIGHT NOW. IF YOU AREN'T SURE, ALLOW ME TO REGALE YOU WITH THE TALE OF MY EXPERIENCE WITH ROAD REDEMPTION.
I watched the trailer for Road Redemption and immediately knew I needed it in my life. I bought and installed it, eagerly awaiting my early access experience, knowing that even if the game doesn't progress beyond its current state, the devs claim that there's already a solid 10-15 hours of gameplay implemented. I believe that this may not be entirely accurate. You can't call this gameplay - this is an
.
My first run, I didn't make it to the end of the first track. I wasn't entirely sure on the controls or mechanics, but it seemed fun enough. Did I mention this is a game with permadeath? If you get a game over, you spend your XP on some permanent upgrades, then it's back to the start. Any unspent XP is discarded. Killing enemies is the best way to tip the odds in your favor here - every kill nets you some boost meter, some health, some XP, and some cash. Cash, and the items you buy with it, are lost when you die. Depending on your playstyle, you may find that you prioritize certain items which complement your playstyle. I advise you to save this approach for later. Become comfortable with both the selection of melee weapons and ranged weapons. Learn how explosives work. Learn to use the grappling hook, once you get it. Did I mention there's a goddamned GRAPPLING HOOK? Learn to parry enemy attacks. Learn to kick other racers into oncoming traffic or environmental obstacles. Learn what shortcuts look like, and when to use them (or not to use them). Learn to use your jump jets, when playing on rooftop levels. Learn to disarm enemies. In short, learn the ins and outs of the game's many and varied mechanics, to ensure your success. Which is never guaranteed, since each run is randomized. Sometimes there are snow levels. Sometimes one of your fellow racers will be driving a car intead of a motorcycle. Sometimes it won't be a car, but a truck filled with logs, which spill out and cause everybody behind you to crash out, completely filling your boost meter. Sometimes there's hallucinogenic gas.
There are still some rough areas of the game - parts of the UI need work, parts of the soundtrack, which is mostly great, is... less great. Sometimes the game will decide that I should be facing the opposite direction in the middle of a race, just for funsies. It also takes too long to get back into the action after crashing out, especially on the rooftop levels. I also kind of find myself yearning for actual graphics options. And unlockable bikes/riders. Those are just little niggles, though,  and the game IS in early access, after all.
In short, if you like combat racing games or the original Road Rash, or just want to play as Shovel Knight riding a motorcycle swinging off of helicopters on a grappling hook and smacking racers with a medieval mace, buy this game. It's really good. Also, it has 4-player co-op, and online coming soon.

If you haven't yet started the Trails Series I highly recommend you do. This is the first game in the series, and therefore the best place to start.
The main selling point of the Trails games is their writing. Both the world and the characters are brilliantly done. The main flaw which follows from this is that especially the first game is very slow paced to begin with. If you can get past that however, you will enjoy what has become my favorite game series of all time. Since it has been some time since this game arrived on steam you luckily do not have to wait before you can play 3 sequels (Trails in the sky SC, the Third and Trails of Cold Steel).  The sequel to Cold Steel should be coming within a few months.
There are a few trails games however which have not been localised from Japan despite being out for quite a long time at this point. This is partially due to the fact these games have ridiculous amounts of dialogue which need translation, but also because the series is not as popular as it deserves to be. By buying games in the series you are contributing to these games one day being translated.
Overall, if you like dialogue oriented games and are not put off by the idea of a slow start, you will almost certainly enjoy this game. Even at its default price this game is a steal in my opinion, and by buying it you are contributing to more of these great games being brought over.

This Game is great if you have 10 bucks to spare, allow me to go into more detail. So we start off with a game that has a very retro feel to it obviously refering to the Oregon Trail which is great because I love these old type of games. The gameplay is good as it allows you to do a lot of activities such as dodging zombie deer or repairing you vehicle. Another thing that is great is all the references to other zombie games/films such as the hand rising out of the ground when you visit a tombstone or at The Church landmark, the scenery is a reenact of an early scene from the film Night of the Living Dead, where a man with glasses is lying on the ground dead, and a blonde woman is fleeing away from a nearby zombie. The soundtrack is great as well with the 8-bit feel with a mix of tensity and a bit of ambience. The artwork for the place you get to like Chicago and The Mall are very well done keeping the retro feel to it. However there are some downsides to it as well. The controls and some of the mechanics can be hard to learn to some players so maybe an option in settings to configure the controls more would help gamers who can't get them down easier. Also I say 10$ at the beggining of the review because the dev's cut some of the great content from the director's cut into a DLC "The Final Cut", so if you're thinking about buying this game have 10$ to do it to buy the DLC to not miss out and some content that makes the game great. I don't know if anyone else is like me, but I used to love platformers. So imagine my confusion upon picking up so many modern, indie platformers and with utter frustration screaming "WHY'S IT SO HARD?! WHAT IS THIS MADNESS?!".
Eventually after I had bought a new monitor to replace the one I had smashed I calmed down and kept hearing about FEZ. Not your standard platformer with enemies and weapons but an explorative one with puzzles.
The creative ideas put into the game make the puzzles wonderful to complete and there are enough of them to always make you feel like you are making some progress rather than just being stuck for hours. The controls feel tight and responsive and the puzzles themselves range from very simple "get here" to.......well.....you might need to brush up on some morse code to solve that one.
I highly reccomend you buy and play this enjoyable title.
Despite the drama surrounding this game, the concept, art and sound design are all brilliant.  This is still easily one of my favorite indie games, and it continues to age well.

This game doesn't cease to give me goosebumps.
Completely ignoring the fantastic storyline, tight controls and amazing mechanics, this game creates a hair-raising atmosphere. The lo-fi electonic tunes coupled with the landscape pull you into the world of FEZ and you'll completely forget you're sitting at your desk playing a video game. I sometimes just wanted to stop and stare at the sunset behind me.
Apart from the atmosphere, the reward system in the game feeds off the storyline. You'll find yourself wanting to explore deeper and deeper, searching for doors to worlds you haven't found yet. And because of the worlds mechanics and the way you interact with them, that's not as easy as you think.
I recommend this game to literally anyone.

Surprisingly, this game derails almost into impossibility in the last chapter. I was getting "A++" on every single level prior to that chapter (requiring a decent amount of retries, of course), even including the encores. But after just a few levels into Chapter 8, I gave up attempting to get those ranks and just wanted to finish the game. The levels really get into more of a hardcore level than I expected from this game.
Regardless of that, I still enjoyed the game for some time, and only really finished the storyline, so there's other parts I haven't tried out. I think that most of the platforming is definitely good, though there are some flaws in the programming. For instance, lasers and moving platforms/obstacles and other pieces do not generate consistent patterns. What this ends up causing sometimes is that you find places where you are stuck, because a laser blocks a platform indefinitely, or multiple lasers will go off at the same time when in fact they should be alternating.
I noticed these issues most often in the last chapter because of the amount of obstacles the developers have in it. An example is a section where these two lasers should be alternating because you have to hold onto rails and either jump over or run under spikes depending upon which laser is going off. I ended up retrying the level a few times, because I had both lasers firing at the same time, making it impossible to move down a pathway. And just as stated above, retrying the level eventually caused the lasers to alternate and made it possible to continue.
I also had issues with the creature that looks like a square pig, which you can use to ride around certain areas. It usually ended up moving away on its own in bad situations, like when I was holding onto a ceiling bar over water and a laser. The laser would fire and the creature would move at some point (not because of damage, since it's invincible), meaning I'd fall into the water.
Despite these issues, it wasn't like they blocked the game or anything for me. I was able to complete the majority of the game with a little work, until that extreme ending chapter requiring me to throw away some goals in order to prevent some stress.
The graphics of the game are pretty good and I like the style of the cardboard cutout/puppet show scenes. I'm relatively familiar with the humor style here, but I played Castle Crashers years ago and that game is a lot less over-the-top than this one. While I found a lot of the stuff funny, including songs and secret rooms, the Narrator got annoying by Chapter 6 onward, which is just a bit over halfway through the game.
If you are not much into platforming or the humor/style in the trailers throws you off, then you probably won't like the game. Otherwise, you'll likely have a decent time with it. It has a good amount of enjoyable mechanics for the platforming and requires some thought in tackling everything quickly. Also, I hate the swarming cat enemies...

This is my first review on steam, so bear with me.
So, I've been casually playing this game for a while now, long before it's release on Steam, and I can happily say that it is my favorite mmorpg. I'm not saying the game is perfect, but it is a lot of fun, especially with a good guild and friends to level with.
Probably the weakest aspect of the game is the questing, which is about as generic as it gets, and the lore isn't anything special. I'm also not a huge fan of the ridiculously skimpy outfits on the female characters, but it is something I can personally look past. Just don't be surprised if you see a tank rushing into battle with her breasts barely covered by a metal bra.
I main a mystic (healing/support class) and I've never had so much fun playing as a healer before, this is coming from someone who usually goes for the healing and support classes in mmos. It's refreshing to see an mmo that doesn't resort to simple point-and-click combat. Most of the races are really cool looking, my personal favorite being the amani race. You can be a little girl with animal ears, a chubby forest creature, a rock monster, and a seductive-looking devil.
I've played a lot of mmos in the past, but I always find myself coming back to TERA. The staff and moderators are really helpful and down-to-earth, and the community is friendly for the most part. I'd also like to add that the game isn't pay2win, so thats a bonus, especially for a free-to-play mmorpg.
If you love mmorpgs, you will likely love TERA.

I have spent a lot of time playing this game. The time of writing this review, I have put in 143 hours. Cities: Skylines is a fun city builder, it allows tonnes of creativity, and is one of the best games I've played for PC.
That said there are a few problems with the game that are so major, I've stopped playing the game. The first problem is that when a city reaches a certain size, my computor struggles to go past 5-6 fps, you really need a beefy computor to run this game. The next problem, and this is the main reason why I stopped playing, is that it takes so long to load. I remember when I first got the game, it took about 3 minutes to load, and I had no mods at all. At its worst it took 15 minutes to load the game, and that was with mods.
Last week, I tried to run the game again, I turned of all my mods (not assets), I started a new city, and it took 10 minutes to load, and then an error message poped-up, I closed it a few times, because sometimes if you click the 'x' button a few times the error will stop occuring, but it  kept happening, and I had to quit the game.
Saying that I do recommend the game, it is still fun, and if you have the hardware, and don't get anything of the workshop, you'll easily have 30 fps.
*Note* It's  also good to ttake into consideration that I play on a laptop, and it's not ment for gaming, so the hardware is low.

The main purpose of this thread is to show my views on the new ban system, as well as alternatives for instant bans / permanent bans. Since there is no appeal system, there are some cases that haven't been taken into account, and I discuss them in my edit below the main thread.
**********************
New ban system is ridiculous.
1. The "Language Ban" list isn't public, so how can you excpect anyone to know what is acceptable to say? Understandably there are obvious words, but some "racial slurs" have other meanings at a school playground, or in different countries.
2. 24 Hour Ban to introduce to the ban system?? Most people play weekends which means that the very first ban accounts for half your weekly gaming! That's equivalent to an 84 hour ban (more than your "second ban" duration).
3. Permanent ban after 4 convictions?!?!? Players invest quite often upwards of 100's of pounds or dollars or euros, and the best answer to bad language used by your community is a permanent ban? I am going to list some alternatives below, that also happen to be more relevant to the offence committed, and it took me 5 minutes to come up with...
4. What is your plan to combat troll parties of 3 that will get players instant banned if they all report at the same time? I have witnessed these troll parties bully people viciously in the past, then when that person gets upset and eventually retaliates they get banned for it. How is a system that allows 3 bullies to overpower 1 innocent player a "fair system"???
Anyway, here is my list of alternative methods;
>A warning report that allows innocent players a chance to correct their mistakes, by suggesting that they don't lash out in anger OR it will result in a 24 hour ban
>Following the previous option, an hour ban instead of a 24 hour ban for the first ban, same reason as prior
>Restricting voice and text chat for players that have abuse *voice and text chat* rather than banning them from the game completely (seen as they still should have the right to access the servers they have paid for, just not the features they have abused)
>Ban count reductions for good behaviour. This means that if you have a certain number of months of not having a ban, then your total ban count gets reduced so that the previous ban doesn't count towards you ultimately getting permanently banned (Everyone deserves the chance to correct their mistakes, and no-one should have to play with the fear of slipping up or even getting a typo)
>An option for you to compete against the ban allegation and tell your side of the story. As I am sure administrators have access to the full chat history and gameplay footage, players could appeal their innocence (for issues such as typo's, bullying and other such issues)
To be honest, with the ban system as it is, Black Ops 3 and Treyarch gives the impression that they support bullying and that they do not appreciate the continual support of their community. This and this alone is the reason for my negative review of the game, and I will be happy to change it once this issue gets fixed.
********EDIT********
Below I am going to list a couple of examples of bans that would need a more sophisticated ban system for justice to be done.
>Replying to a question with 'You cant' but accidentally mistyping the 'a'. The suggestion here is that someone is reporting you before you can correct yourself in chat, so the admin in charge of banning you has no idea that it was a typo.
>Forgetting that your discord push to talk and Black Ops 3 push to talk are the same button, so whilst someone ingame thinks you are hurling abuse at them you are actually just sharing a back and forth with your mates in a different app. Now I don't know how the verbal harrasment system works, because Treyarch won't tell us, but if it is a stacking up of reports that gets you banned then this innocent mistake would contribute to that.
>A younger player asking the meaning of a word they have just read / heard. I have personally seen this happen ingame a lot. The context for this one is that the original offender can choose when to report the young player meaning their comment won't be in the report. (This is a double problem since whilst the innocent / curious young player gets banned, the original offender can continue playing Black Ops 3 happily).
Now I know that there are other variants of these examples, and probably some examples that I haven't covered, but I think these cover the main ones. I am also happy that there is a system to ban the cruel / toxic players on the game to improve the community, but I believe there needs to be a way to distinguish between the cruel and the innocent. The ban system needs to be less abusable by those with malintent.
Thanks for all of the support so far! (Please be respectful to those stating their views in the comments as I am sure you would expect respect in return)

Pony Island is a story-rich and addictive and had me camped for 5 hours straight. In those five hours, I was mind-♥♥♥♥ed, visually stunned and left wanting more. If you're into psychological horror/creepy♥♥♥♥♥♥and devastatingly hard but infinitely enjoyable puzzles, this is for you.

I will admit that this is not the game for everyone; however,  this is still one of the best indie games I have ever played and only wish I would have been exposed to the game sooner.  The gameplay is incredibly well balanced and the mechanics are phenomenal, especially considering the scale of the project.  I was shocked by the leg and tentacle animations, which remain fluid and realistic.  Also, the soundtrack is incredible (10/10 would buy if for sale).
PROS:
-Sold as advertised (i.e. not misrepresented)
-Awesome music
-Effective graphics (though simple, the style conveys actions and details surprisingly well)
-Balanced gameplay
-Easy to learn, hard to master
-Variety in parts and A.I. fleets
-Environmental factors
-Creative universe (i.e. well designed and unique)
-Individualization of gameplay
-Low cost (compared to, say, Avorion)
CONS:
-Missions are more extensions of the tutorial
-Conquer mode can be simplistic at times, random at others
-Targeting system, especially boarders and planes, could use some improvements (note: this is not to say make module targeting possible, but maybe module type)
-Occasional glitches/crashes (rare or non-obstructive)
Grade: A (90-95%)

tl;dr right up front. TERA is a pretty fun MMO.
Throughout the game the visuals are pretty amazing, just look at my gallery for this game. The actiony gameplay and impressive visuals do have to make up for a fairly grindy progression system, but if you actually do take the time to read the quests they are usually pretty interesting. I leveled up several characters in this game and each time took an entirely different progression because there's tons and tons of content, more than you could possibly ever see.
This is originally a Korean game so there are a few eccentricities that you do have to overlook compared to a western game. One of the most jarring is probably the revamped storyline. Sometimes things seem to make little sense and that's often because they were adjusted for western audiences by amateur writers, voice over work for npcs and cutscenes were done with absolutely no care for context. Had they put more care into those elements this game would've drawn a much larger audience, but I'm sure there were budget constraints. It's not terrible, but it's simply good enough to be passable.
As far as the cash shop is concerned, this game is certainly not pay to win. While there are some minor stat boosting things in the shop they are very minor and nowhere are they needed or required by anyone in the game. There are however loads and loads of convinience and cosmetics, and in a game so heavily focused on aesthetics why wouldn't there be? You really don't need a sub, it just brings you convinience. Where they do make their money is the cash shop. You can be sure they will have something you want, if only because it's wicked cool looking. Stay away from the random packs which are clearly a trap for people with deep pockets. Only buy items that are guranteed to be what you want.
Finally there's the overly sexual nature of every character in the game (Except a few oddball NPC's that stand out for wearing normal clothing and the Popori). Now for me, I grew up reading fantasy books with elaborate Boris Vallejo covers and older tales of Greek mythology. I can definately see how some people are shocked, simply shocked, to find armors that leave almost a whole pixel boob on screen. For me this is a non issue for the most part, I have no problem with the bare 8 pack of a Castanic male or the heaving boobs of the Elven queen.
But then there's the Elin.
The Elin race are a little too 'childlike' to be wearing some of the overly sexual stuff they have available to them, even if they're really 'nature spirits' or whatever. Elin are probably the most popular race in the game and I'm sure not every one of them is a sexual predator, most are girls wanting to play something cute. Sadly most is not all. They are little anime girl equivalents to the small comedic races in other games and it really would've been fine if they were left as comic characters, but when you see a herd of them run past (they DO move in herds!) wearing lingerie it is extremely uncomfortable.
That's about it. I have about 8 or so characters in this game, but I've entirely quit playing myself. Not because I didn't enjoy the overall experience, I just have moved on to newer things. Could it be done better? Probably. Are you going to be entertained? Definately. Will it cost you anything to take a look? Nope.

Assassin's Creed III is by no means the best of the franchise, but it's still worth your time, especially if you're a fan.
I don't think anyone watched the trailers, teasers, or TV spots more than me; I was pumped for this game. I loved Ezio's story, but I was ready for a new man in new robes and in a new era. Colonial America in the midst of revolutionary war? Yes! George Washington and Benjamin Franklin? Sign me up! An actual bow with arrows? I can't wait! Combat was also promised an upgrade with the new ability to dual wield weapons (which included a very cool-looking tomahawk). And did I mention the hunting?
My initial reaction was a negative one, I'm sad to report. The disjointed story, lack of character development, and the overly long "tutorial" portion of the game in addition to the protagonist, a half-English and half-Native American named Ratonhnhaké:ton (or simply Connor), being unlikable and unrelatable, was all disappointing to me. A previous reviewer called this game a "well-crafted mess" and I think this is the most apt description I've heard so far. Everything about it screams "epic" and it feels like they really had something big planned for the game, but there was a breakdown in communication somewhere in development and the end-product just didn't meet everyone's expectations. According to an Ubisoft employee, there were too many cooks in the kitchen. That's not to say this game is bad, it just means that it wasn't as good as it could have been, and it's nowhere near the level of its predecessors.
Skip to the last paragraph for closing statements if you haven't played the game.
Let's start with the story. It just doesn't "pull" you in and it never reaches a point where you think, "Wow. This is awesome." AC II had you invade Vatican City and use Da Vinci's flying machine to glide over the towers of Venice. AC Brotherhood had you scale the ancient walls of the Colosseum and columns of pagan temples. AC Revelations (the arguably weakest of the three) even had you returning to Masyaf castle--stronghold of the Assassins in Altaïr's time--in the first "DNA sequence." But what do we do in this installment? Well, at one point, you run from point on point on a battlefield in a very linear, arranged fashion, trying not to get mowed down by the British army (the army that you decimate single-handed in the cinematic trailer). You also do a lot of pouting... and asking where a certain Mr. Lee might be located (on one occasion, he's simply sitting behind you). Additionally, there's Paul Revere, who rides your horse so he can warn the Patriots of an impending British attack, whose instructions can be interpreted as "annoying."
In my opinion, the game shines when the story is focused on Haythem Kenway, Connor's father, and his motives for his behavior and his interactions with his son. Where's Charles Lee? I don't know and I don't care. Haythem, a character you play during the first few sequences, is a fascinating man and one we should have seen more of. His ending was tragic, not because of who it involved, but because of who he was fighting for. Why was Lee the one to lead the colonies to a Templar-friendly future? Why couldn't Kenway, the patently better man, do this? I either couldn't follow the logic or some important moments in the story were left on the cutting room floor in the rush to meet the release date. The rest of the Templar baddies were one-dimensional villains who get picked off one-by-one just like in the other games and they're not even committed Templars. I did find Lee to be an interesting antagonist, though he makes all the classic villain mistakes ("I will watch him suffer and kill him later!"). I also enjoyed the homestead and naval missions, though I felt like trading and crafting were a waste of my time; it never felt like I needed money--Connor doesn't wear armor nor does he require anything that can't be looted off a body.
I love the new stealth elements. Connor has the ability to hide behind corners and in tall grass and brush and lure enemies to their deaths by means of whistling. I feel this was sorely needed and I hope they add more ways of killing clandestinely in future installments.
This game was a fresh vision for the Assassin's Creed series, which was growing a bit overly serious and stale by the end of Revelations. The formula of starting over in a new city, reclaiming it from Templar influence, and inducting forgettable minions into the Order to assist you in missions was growing tiresome. All that considered, I very much appreciate what they attempted to do with this game and the direction it's going. Connor may be unlikable, but that doesn't mean he wasn't a good character, and he's part of the Kenway story. Recommended.

** This game gets incredibly grindy towards the last half of the game and kind of loses the management sim aspect of the first half, so dont buy if you dont want to grind out numbers**
If i hadnt already fell in love with the over the top ridiculously 80's feel (In the options you can make the game have retro pixelated graphics for the real 80's arcade vibe) along with all of the little refrences to good movies, comics, TV shows and games i would have an entirely different opinion on how good or bad this game is.  The first half of the game is where it really shines as a management sim / rpg / glorified rock'em sock'em robots spectator sport.  Unfortunately the last half of the game loses its perspective and just turns into watching numbers go up and down until you get the ones you need to beat the other guys higher numbers taking all of the skill out of it.  If the Devs would lower the amount of points you lose per day and make the game less grindy it would double the fun factor but they wouldnt want people to finish their game in like 2 or 3 hours so they'll never do that.
I will note though that the game is a lesson that to become physically fit and stay in shape you constantly need to train in different areas and make sure not to get complacent just grinding out the same thing.  If you ever go to a gym you'll hear they have things like "Arm day" or "Leg day" you alternate just enough to build on the muscles a day or so prior. If you abscent mindedly look around waiting while your guy trains he will start gaining less and less from doing that activity and use more food/energy doing it. What you need to do is cycle through the whole gym doing a little bit of each to keep the gains high and burning through food and energy low.  This may confuse some people that play the game thinking that its just showing you how much time you have left on that workout, but the developer has confirmed that you are in fact LOSING a percentage of each gained bubble.
I didnt expect this game to subtlety try and teach you how to work out effectively. I also didnt expect how damn difficult it is to buy and keep food in the fridge when your also trying to stay the most physically fit for your upcoming fights. You also may have to swap out your abilities mid fight because while your stamina is high the other guy may be doing way waaaay more damage and dumping all your defensive ♥♥♥♥ in order to push for the win is the best course of action,  Each skill tree has something that counteracts the other two so making sure your not taking block when the guy your going up against has something that goes through 40% of your blocked damage. Taking the time between rounds to switch out these things and seeing what works will net you a solid victory and not get your ♥♥♥ whooped.
This game says to me that to stay still or to put your nose to the grinder is the worst thing to do so to avoid that you need to step back, assess your options, try to keep an open mind and dont get tunnel vision....like a real fighter. A true fighter is not a mindless emotionless thug but a well oiled machine that is more a lifestyle and less a interest or hobby you watch on UFC because everyones on the bandwagon.
Overall its a fun game for $10 but if you are the type of person who was looking for a deep game that needs constant attention being a fighters coach you would be barking up the wrong tree.  Its more of a Ipad type game that you'd play on the toilet.  As i said at the start if spending days and days grinding out numbers would bore you to tears id steer clear of this game too.  Its a charming casual rock'em sock'em robots game that just needs a hip 80's kid with spikey hair to play it in a commercial.

What an awesome game PUNCH CLUB is. Take the Rocky series, 16 bit retro graphics, a pinch of the Sims, a good storyline and great game mechanics and you have the best indie game I've played in 2016.

Feed him, get him a job, try and jungle between training sessions, love interests, learn new tricks, it's all about how you manage to choose your priorities. There's many possibilities and the skill tree offers tons of options, as well as specialities. Very interesting on a tactical level, well balanced and actually quite hard, the progression is quite a challenge.
When the fight starts, you just have to sit back and hope for the best. You can still change a couple of tactical moves between rounds but you'll find yourself in a situation pretty similar to the Football Manager series. It's only about having a good game plane and the best preparation you can afford because once the gloves are on, there's nothing you can do to prevent your guy going down.
Best moment in the game was after an hour play, I'm yelling at my screen and encouraging Johnny, totally into the match.
It's pretty addictive and compelling.

Highlights: Nostalgia, Sound and Gameplay
I've spent hundreds and hundreds of hours on this game way, way back when it was first released. This game, Age of Empires II, and Starcraft I were the only games I played for months. I challenged many friends, tested out multiple strategies, perfected my aim, and created multiple schemes and maps. This game will always hold a special place in my gaming experiences.
Anyways, the gameplay of this Worms game is probably the best in the series. I'm not just saying that due to nostalgia. After playing Worms 3D, Worms 2 Armageddon, Worms Reloaded, Worms 4 Mayhem, Worms Revolution, Worms Open Warfare, and so on, those all feel inferior to the classic gameplay shown in Worms Armageddon. Bazooka in particular has always felt just write on the 2D landscape in this game. But things like traversing the landscape, setting up traps, and strategizing combos worked well within this gameplay style.
Character customization is as charming as ever. The worms voices and sounds are still fantatically presented. The graphics are also better than what I remember from the 15 year old game.
Overall, this is one game I'll always cherish and looking forward to more zany battles with these dastardly invertebrates.

After playing this game for five hours in a single day, I’m really tired. I think I actually ruined the game for myself by playing it for so long in one sitting. If so, I might have to come back to this one later. Anyways, here’s my review of BattleBlock Theater.
The story starts of on a ship, where a lot of friends go on adventures together. One day, a heavy storm hits the ship, and they get shipwrecked on a seemingly abandoned island. Once you wake up, you’ll find a theater. When you enter the theater, you’re quickly captured by some cats, and forced to go through some deadly obstacle courses to entertain the cats. Worst of all, the leader of the cats is non other than your best friend, Hatty Hattington! Every time you beat a world, a cutscene will play that will tell you more about the story, hilariously narrated by Stamper. The story might not be that interesting, but the cutscenes are really funny! It’s worth going through just for the jokes!
Overall, this game looks pretty good. While there is a lot of the same blocks and enemies, that’s actually a good thing. Every object looks quite different from each other, so you’ll always know what a block will do when you see it. “Look! a lava block. That means that if I jump on it it will send me flying!” So even though the objects look exactly the same through the entire game, It would be much more annoying if they changed it, because then you'd have to learn the new design.
One of the best things about this game, is that you can change the appearance of your character. You can buy new heads in the shop. There’s a lot of heads, I mean A LOT! There’s some really funny ones in there, and I loved to try and find the best ones! I wish there was a random head option though, since it takes time to change it. I ended up using the same head for most of the game.
the music is  really good! There’s a lot of songs I’ve had in my head that I forgot came from this game. I’ve had the main theme in my head for the last couple of days. I’m not very good at describing music, so the best way I can describe it is wacky. Take a listen to the secret area song, and see what i mean! I just realized that It might not be the best example for the game. listen to the boss stage music if you want to hear how the music of this game is!
This game is a platformer game. If you don’t like platformers, this isn’t gonna change your mind. On every stage, you’ll have to collect three gems to continue to the next stage. The gems also works as currency for buying new heads. Every stage has six or seven gems, and you’ll most likely get the required amount before reaching the end. There’s also balls of yarn to collect, one on each stage. These can be used to buy new weapons. You can have two weapons on you, and some of them are really useful! My favorite is the frog bomb, which can be used as a platform, and you can reach places you're not supposed to be in yet! The level design starts off pretty good. the first four worlds are a blast! but then comes the second half.
My problem with the second half is the level design. The levels go from some really good platforming, to puzzles. Lots and lots of puzzles. I don’t have a big problem with puzzles in platformers. Doing it right, it could be a nice change of phase. Battleblock Theater however, does not do it right. The levels get huge and convoluted. I spent a long time not knowing where to go! The levels get so confusing, that when I finished them, I had no idea how! Instead of enjoying the game the last two hours, I had to pull myself through the last two worlds. I didn’t enjoy myself! At least the cutscenes were entertaining.
Even though I’ve only played multiplayer for an hour, It is my favorite part of the game! Every level is remade into a multiplayer version, where you have to cooperate to make it through the level. I’ve only played the first world in multiplayer, but it’s so much fun! If I’m gonna replay the game later, it will be in multiplayer. One problem I have is that when I was trying to find some random person to play with, the loading thing would just spin around endlessly! I waited three minutes, but nothing happened! Well, I feel like local is the best way to play anyways, since then you can actually communicate with the one you’re playing with. There are some pvp modes I haven’t tested yet, but will pretty soon.
I forgot to talk about the level creation. I haven’t given it a real shot yet, since I suck at creating levels, but it’s cool that it’s there. You can also play other peoples levels, so you basically have endless amount of gameplay in this game!
One little thing I want to talk about, is WHY THE HELL IS THE YES BUTTON RED? Red symbolises NO. In every other game in the universe, when in a menu, green is yes, and red is no. But not in this one, oh no. I had to recalibrate my brain when playing this game, because when I wanted to restart a level, I always pressed no, since it was green!
I have mixed feelings about this game. While the presentation is amazing, and the gameplay is fun, I was annoyed through last two hours! It was not an enjoyable experience! Even so, I still think this game deserves a
7/10
While I didn’t enjoy myself the last few hours, the first four worlds were really fun! I was gonna give it a six, but mix in an amazing multiplayer, a level creator, and being able to play other peoples levels, this game suddenly feels much better! Plus, the humor and music is great! I would give it a 6/10 or maybe even 5/10 if you’re planning to play this alone, but grab with you a friend, and you will have a good time!

The main purpose of this thread is to show my views on the new ban system, as well as alternatives for instant bans / permanent bans. Since there is no appeal system, there are some cases that haven't been taken into account, and I discuss them in my edit below the main thread.
**********************
New ban system is ridiculous.
1. The "Language Ban" list isn't public, so how can you excpect anyone to know what is acceptable to say? Understandably there are obvious words, but some "racial slurs" have other meanings at a school playground, or in different countries.
2. 24 Hour Ban to introduce to the ban system?? Most people play weekends which means that the very first ban accounts for half your weekly gaming! That's equivalent to an 84 hour ban (more than your "second ban" duration).
3. Permanent ban after 4 convictions?!?!? Players invest quite often upwards of 100's of pounds or dollars or euros, and the best answer to bad language used by your community is a permanent ban? I am going to list some alternatives below, that also happen to be more relevant to the offence committed, and it took me 5 minutes to come up with...
4. What is your plan to combat troll parties of 3 that will get players instant banned if they all report at the same time? I have witnessed these troll parties bully people viciously in the past, then when that person gets upset and eventually retaliates they get banned for it. How is a system that allows 3 bullies to overpower 1 innocent player a "fair system"???
Anyway, here is my list of alternative methods;
>A warning report that allows innocent players a chance to correct their mistakes, by suggesting that they don't lash out in anger OR it will result in a 24 hour ban
>Following the previous option, an hour ban instead of a 24 hour ban for the first ban, same reason as prior
>Restricting voice and text chat for players that have abuse *voice and text chat* rather than banning them from the game completely (seen as they still should have the right to access the servers they have paid for, just not the features they have abused)
>Ban count reductions for good behaviour. This means that if you have a certain number of months of not having a ban, then your total ban count gets reduced so that the previous ban doesn't count towards you ultimately getting permanently banned (Everyone deserves the chance to correct their mistakes, and no-one should have to play with the fear of slipping up or even getting a typo)
>An option for you to compete against the ban allegation and tell your side of the story. As I am sure administrators have access to the full chat history and gameplay footage, players could appeal their innocence (for issues such as typo's, bullying and other such issues)
To be honest, with the ban system as it is, Black Ops 3 and Treyarch gives the impression that they support bullying and that they do not appreciate the continual support of their community. This and this alone is the reason for my negative review of the game, and I will be happy to change it once this issue gets fixed.
********EDIT********
Below I am going to list a couple of examples of bans that would need a more sophisticated ban system for justice to be done.
>Replying to a question with 'You cant' but accidentally mistyping the 'a'. The suggestion here is that someone is reporting you before you can correct yourself in chat, so the admin in charge of banning you has no idea that it was a typo.
>Forgetting that your discord push to talk and Black Ops 3 push to talk are the same button, so whilst someone ingame thinks you are hurling abuse at them you are actually just sharing a back and forth with your mates in a different app. Now I don't know how the verbal harrasment system works, because Treyarch won't tell us, but if it is a stacking up of reports that gets you banned then this innocent mistake would contribute to that.
>A younger player asking the meaning of a word they have just read / heard. I have personally seen this happen ingame a lot. The context for this one is that the original offender can choose when to report the young player meaning their comment won't be in the report. (This is a double problem since whilst the innocent / curious young player gets banned, the original offender can continue playing Black Ops 3 happily).
Now I know that there are other variants of these examples, and probably some examples that I haven't covered, but I think these cover the main ones. I am also happy that there is a system to ban the cruel / toxic players on the game to improve the community, but I believe there needs to be a way to distinguish between the cruel and the innocent. The ban system needs to be less abusable by those with malintent.
Thanks for all of the support so far! (Please be respectful to those stating their views in the comments as I am sure you would expect respect in return)

Tera is a breath of fresh air among the free-to-play MMO titles available. I'll briefly detail what keeps me playing in hopes that I can convince you to join in the fun.
It's one part traditional MMORPG combat and one part action. Attacks and skills can be chained for combos and enemy attacks and skills can be dodged/blocked/countered too. Of course, they have to hit to be effective! It might feel a bit repetitive in PvE due to the fact that it's super easy to learn the timing of monster attacks, but PvP is where combat really shines. I was never much of a PvPer, but I got into it just because the combat super fun.
There's a plethora of different classes to play, and most of them have a unique feel and style to them. For example, the Brawler class which favors fast paced, up-close and personal beatdowns is going to handle much differently than the Gunner, a medium-ranged tank that rains fire on enemies. They play just as differently as they sound, and having lots of classes to try out keeps me from getting bored.
This one's HUGE for me. In almost any MMORPG I've played, the game is dominated by wallet warriors who spent real money to have the top tier gear. Usually, the game makes it exponentially easier for people to get said badass gear by busting open their wallets in the cash shop, either through offering high-end materials needed for crafting the best gear or even being audacious enough to outright sell the gear itself. Not in Tera! Here, the almost every major purchase is cosmetic. The only advantages offered are boosts to EXP and gold, mainly for grinding and raiding purposes. No wallet warriors here!

So far I've seen a community free of scammers and bots. It's a generally friendly and helpful environment and it's really contributed to my overall emjoyment. This is especially impressive given how long Tera has been running. No doubt the environment will help any newcomer ease themselves into the community to enjoy the game.
Besides the key features mentioned above, Tera has some beautiul environments, impressive animations for skills, and overall generally pleasing audio and visuals. There really aren't any major downfalls I've encountered so far. Only real con I've had is that the story is pretty weak, but that's what they've got the roleplay servers for. If you're tired of playing the same-old pay-to-win MMOs over and over again, definitely come and give Tera a try!

It's just a better city simulation game than EA's Simcity.

There has been some debate recently regarding the annual release schedule of the Assassin’s Creed franchise. Some people argue that churning out a new game every year lessens the quality of the franchise. They equate it to modern war games like Call of Duty or Battlefield. Where I stand is: if putting out games every year didn’t make the companies as much money as it does, they wouldn’t do it. It’s our fault for buying every new Assassin’s Creed that comes out. Also, you have to remember that Ubisoft is a huge company. They do have several projects running simultaneously, just because it’s been a year since the last game came out does nt mean that the new game has only been in development for 12 months.
By now, just about everyone and their axolotl knows about Assassin’s Creed III, the “hell yes! America!” game. I’ve heard a lot of criticism about ACIII but I don’t think it deserves all of it. Yes, the game is one of the glitchiest things I’ve ever played. Boston and New York aren’t as distinguishable as previous cities in the franchise. There aren’t many, if any, decent free-running paths in the cities. There are some interesting tree paths in the frontier but running through the trees feels slower than how free-running was in previous games.  Combat was improved, in my opinion, though if you’re fighting too many blokes at once there are times when the combat indicators just won’t work. I like how the counter has had the turtling aspect removed so that there is a little bit of skill involved. The ship missions have also been the target of many a displeased comment, but I really enjoyed them and they seem to have based Black Flag completely off of the ship missions.
The weakest link of ACIII is the modern day sequences. But Desmond has always been a shaking foundation to build the franchise on. In ACIII it feels like there was a huge buildup for a giant flop. What I really don't like is that Desmond is just a reskinned Connor. It feels like the developers completely forgot that the point of having the Desmond in ACII was to train him through the bleeding effect of the animus. Logically he should still run, climb and fight like Ezio did, not have an instant shift to Connor. It even goes as far as Desmond fights with a second knife that magically appears from the ether.
ACIII has an interesting story. I was impressed that Connor never chose a side in the revolution. He has reason enough to dislike the British and the Patriots. He is actually fighting for his people’s safety, not for the Patriots. The Templars are aiding the British so it becomes the old adage, ‘the enemy of my enemy is my friend.’ Maybe I’m biased because I adore Native culture; I’ve even been mistaken for a Native person (though only from racist comments). It’s true; ACIII is no ACII, which is my personal favourite of the franchise. It also isn’t Assassin’s Creed Revelations which is arguably the worst. I’d place ACIII somewhere between the first Assassin’s Creed game and Brotherhood. It really isn’t a bad game; definitely give it a try, especially the DLC. The episodic gameplay style of The Tyranny of King Washington was extremely enjoyable. The animal spirit power thing actually helped with stealth gameplay. If you have the chance pick up Assassin’s Creed III and see how you like it for yourself but if have a choice between III and Black Flag go with Black Flag, please.

This game has been in my backlog for about 2 years and I just managed to complete it recently. The only regret I have is that I didn't finish the game earlier so I'll have more time on the other 2 games in this trilogy.
I don't write reviews for games and this is actually my first, but I think enough has been said by other reviewers that this game is a gem. I won't go on about reviewing the actual game but instead I'll detail on why I completed it after leaving this game in my backlog after these years and hopefully some will be inspired to get this game off your backlog as well.
This game landed in my backlog as the story had a really slow start as each chapter has its own self contained story that wraps up relatively well at the end. The story paces itself well for each chapter but loses momentum when trasitioning between the early chapters (namely chapters 1-2 and 2-3). Unfortunately that was what left this game in my backlog, the early chapters feel like the story arcs of animes like One Piece, they felt disconnected at the start and I lost interest after completing chapter 2.
That only applies for the early chapters as chapter 3 and 4 is when the story ramps up and links the previous chapters together with returning characters and tying together previous plot points, this is where I got hooked into the story again and boy, the climax of the story is intense. However the story could not have held by itself without the character development and world building done so wonderfully in the early chapters. Without them, I don't think anyone would have cared much for the characters or the political climate of Liberl in the late chapters and that is what made the story at the end so much better.
TLDR:
All in all, great story, great soundtrack, great dialogues, not so great transitioning between early chapters. Get this game off your backlog. If not, get the game, appreciate the slow start as an introduction to the characters and the world, enjoy the end.

One of the finest games I have played on the JRPG genre.
The game is set in the fictional Liberl Kingdom, part of a continent known as Zemuria. The two main protagonists, siblings Estelle Bright and Joshua Bright left their hometown to become official Bracers, individual combat specialists with investigation skills who help those around with various problems.
The basic plot I wrote above doesn't really give the overall plot justice. The writing is solid. The game world feels very detailed and alive. Every character has their own stories, history, ambitions, and social connections. Not one story-related character felt like they were just there. The plot had many interesting twists, turns, and characters you wouldn't expect to play such an integral role.
And heck even the NPCs have their own names and day to day dilemmas. As you journey through the game's world, any event that gets triggered can change what every NPC says.
The plot's pacing can be... slow... not a lot of action happens until chapter 2, it will slow down and pick up again after the half of chapter 3 and then it's all-out until the ending. Though each event has a lot of good build up before happening, in my opinion. The game has five chapters in total.
It can be too wordy, so expect reading a LOT of dialogue. This is both a good thing and bad thing depending on the player's perspective and attention span. Though if you're the type who likes to read and is interested in the lore, then by all means indulge on the vast variety of flavor text this game has to offer.
Given the game's nature of being an RPG, dialogue is also its strongest suite. It's just the right amount of balance between elements of light-hearted comedy, seriousness, dark overtones and drama. I really love the interactions between the characters. I find myself chuckling at Estelle's bants, especially towards Olivier. Actually, everyone in this game has a problem with Olivier, because he's ♥♥♥♥ing gay.
As a side note: This game is legendary for the huge amount of effort it took to translate in English. The game has a whooping 3 million Japanese characters used.
The musical score is fantastic. Especially the game's main theme song, Hoshi no Arika, which is pretty GOAT. I find myself humming to the tune. Composed by Hideaki Kamada, vocals by u-mi, and music by Falcom JDK Band. The song has been reprised by various artists, including Chihiro Yonekura.
The gameplay/combat in Trails in the Sky takes place on a grid and is turn-based. The character's turn order is determined by a tracker called the AT Bar. During the character's turn, the player will be presented with a battle menu (as with many standard RPGs), which you can choose to move, make an attack, use crafts and S-Crafts, or cast orbal arts.
Crafts and S-Crafts are character specific skills with a variety of effects such as cancelling an opposing enemy's casting time, dealing double damage, stat buffs or debuffs, completely heal or revive fallen allies, and even interrupt the battle order of the AT Bar.
Arts or Orbal Arts are the magic spells in this game. We can refer to it as the 'quartz system'. A party member can utilize a multitude of arts depending on the user's orbment aptitude, the number of quartz installed and the total elemental value. This means you can customize the spells a specific character can cast. The quartz system is flexible, allowing characters to take on different roles at different stages of the game. Flexibility is needed in some situations. It is a major game mechanic that will determine whether a dungeon exploration will be fun and exciting, or just flat-out tedious and frustrating.
The graphics are honestly nothing to write home about. I can describe it as isometrical, pseudo-3D. Pretty decent stuff. And note that it is a game released during 2004, back in Japan.
And with that, I end my review of this game.
Buy or Pass? Definitely a must-buy.

I was not exactly expecting much when offered to beta test a game by someone with the same name as the game.  After idling for cards one day, I forgot about the game entirely for a month or two.
Then I felt guilty and decided to fire it up, figuring I would quit after 30 seconds and move on.
I did not expect to get sucked in immediately.  Particularly as I have not liked a racing game since the early 1990s.
This game is a great balance of absurdist action fun and enjoyable racing; even trying to do something as simple as watching for cars barrelling straight at you while you also try to maneuver into the perfect position to club a nearby racer to death proves excellently challenging.
But what really seals the deal of this being a game worth playing is the reward system--receiving cash at the end of every race that you can use for temporary upgrades, and then experience upon death (based on your successes in the races) that can be used for permanent upgrades, is a pretty addictive system.  It certainly kept me playing longer than I expected, and I found myself planning out my next upgrades without even realizing it.
So, overall, a racing game worth playing for people who hate racing games--probably even for people who love racing games!

Love the game due to Road Rash, but this game could use some improvements. In the large scheme of things the game is awesome - mayhem on the road, on a motorcycle, with a weapon. It's the minute details that need a little tweaking in this game. I liked the screams and grunts when you hit people in the original Road Rash. If you're going to create a game about mayhem on the road, you should have that. Variety is deeply needed - variety in the courses, variety in the riders, variety in the motorcycles. I don't like that when my motorcycle is fully upgraded that there is no visible difference. Also, no choppers? I'm a motorcycle guy, and choppers wouldn't stand a chance in a race, but they're so iconic, why not have them---there's just so much more that could be done with the motorcycle designs --- the recent light cycle that was actually created from the Tron movie in real life as a bonus motorcycle? Anything? It would make sense to have a visible difference in the motorcycle if it has fully achieved the next level. The game itself is awesome, the minute details need a lot of tweeking to take this game further. The motorcycles, courses, and riders sorely lack any variety, which will kill the replay value. The roof level is horrific too. Why not have courses on a freeway, in a green country, on the coast, just look at Mario Kart for inspiration as to the location of the courses...anything but roofs...., but maybe I just haven't made it far enough in the game to get past desert and roofs. Also, the lack of the ability to choose the course and the nature of the course (race, take down the gang, take down the cops) is a bit of a bummer. Would be awesome if you could pick the course and choose what the goal of the course will be. Seems like the latter should be easy to accomplish, and it would greatly increase the replay value.

Players Beware, This isn't a typical road rash clone. The level progression can be a little like Road Rash Jailbreak if any one still remembers that.
You get so far into the game, and once you get a game over, You have to start all the way back to square one.
This game is a little more lenient because you can gain XP to level up your skill tree. One Notch on the tree is to start from level 3 instead of level 1.
A solid Check point system would be way better than having to buy them by failing Countless amounts of times.
The AI can be really aggressive in some areas and really hard to complete the objective. Once you run out of super Melees, It's almost impossible to Knock the AI's Off their bikes In the Eliminate X amount of Opponents.
In Road rash and other games, if you countered at the right time you got to take their weapons from them and stun them for a second making the progression doable. In Road Redemption you just dodge, and hope a gang of 10 other Bikers and Cops Don't Knock you out instantly sending you all the way back to either level one or the last purchased check point.
The item system, though Unique makes the game interesting. There is a choice of Guns or melee weapons, like shovels, axes, bats ect.
The bad thing is aiming while steering the bike. The environments can be so chaotic it makes the guns hard to use. So i don't. The weapons have health, so when they are depleted, you can't fight back or counter once you exhaust your last weapon.
The weapons also Auto cycle when you knock out another biker. So if you like a particular weapon be prepared to get the next thing that comes your way.
I like the health system concept this game has going for it and the screen affects when you have low health. You can Gain a little bit of health by knocking out other AI's. The bad, is in the Game mode where you have to take out X number of opponents. They tend to Clump together and gang up on you. Even The AI's that don't have cursors over their heads, and some of the other Cars.

The controls need more polishing, Needs a better turning radius. There is no way to make sharp turns, you have slowing down. There are some areas where you have to slow way down, or you will crash into a mountain or drive over it and fly out into the rest of the unpopulated map.

Road redemption is a game available on steam for Early access and while the game is not fully complete, I feel it is the closest thing you will get to a more modern Road Rash game.
EA has a track record of killing off their companies like Westwood and Maxis.
So as far as hopes of a decent Road Rash being put on any other platform besides the Genesis or Windows 98 is probably a lost hope.
Thankfully Road Redemption seems to be one of the better attempts.
While the game is a more pricey indie title, if you are interested in Motorcycle combat games, this is right down your alley.
The game is developed by several individuals -Developer: Dark Seas Interactive , The Fisch Brothers , Pixel Dash Studios , Fish Factory Games
Early access means this game is going to offer consistant updates until a finished product, but currently at this time the game supports achievements, controllers, and new game + modes which allow the continual playing of the game.
Fun at it’s core, Road Redmption hardly can be considered a hard core story driven game.
The game features a few different charecters including a Shovel Knight skin, but that is all they are just skins.
The difficulty determines the speed of the game and damage values, but I found the default to be just fine.
Playing through the beginning of the game is pretty simple, albeit a bit more difficult depending on the level, later on  the difficulty does crank up though.
The player can invest in upgrades while going through the game, but only while playing, once it’s game over all the money used for perment upgrades and XP is lost.
There are also standard upgrades for level to level use like extra life’s, damage, or healing damage.
Weapons are a bigger part of this game than the actual bikes honestly, though most of them are identicle from the pipe to the sword, they really almost feel the same.
Guns are available in the game and take a huge learning curve to learn, aiming and shooting is difficult to say the least, but the most effective way of dealing with enemies.
Cops and other drivers make an appearance as well, and attempt to chance the player down at any given chance.
Random crashes do occur frequently and can throw you off your game often, making it difficult to just race and have fun.
Overall though, the game is fun and grants multiple levels to play through as of now.
I am also told multiplayer will be coming soon as well.
I would recommend this game to anyone familiar with Road Rash or racing games in general, but not to anyone who is un interested in violent games.
I hope you guys enjoyed this review, and I am signing out.

I run the Feral Interactive port of F1 2015 in Xubuntu (17.10) using the default mesa/amdgpu driver that is included in the linux kernel/ubuntu repository. This is my first F1 sim, so I cannot compare to prior Codemasters F1 games. I have logged 157 hours in this sim and thought it is well past time to give it a review. I am very much a beginner to F1 sim racing and I am coming at this review as a complete noob. Because F1 2017 has been out for a while, I doubt this review will be of use to anyone except for a fellow GNU/Linux user who has an interest in it for whatever reason.
I do my races in regular Championship season mode, medium AI, 60 minute practices, full qualifying, and 100% race lengths.
Self-Built System
CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 1600
RAM: 16Gb DDR4 2400
GPU: AMD RX 460
Steering Wheel: Logitech G29
Installation was via steam and was a breeze
I find F1 2015 to be quite demanding in system resources on budget system hardware similar to mine. I can run the sim on medium quality settings with 16x anistropic filtering and disabled TAA/SMAA with FPS in the 50's. F1 2015 is more demanding on system resources than Dirty Rally and GRID Autosport. I do not have F1 2017, so I cannot compare to this sim.
For a first-time F1 sim racer, I find there is quite a lot to like in F1 2015. Visually, F1 2015 is quite a nice sim to experience. The colors are bright. The environments are detailed. The cars have a good look to them.
A feature I particularly enjoy is the dynamic weather system. It is pretty cool beginning a race in dry conditions, gradually moving to wet conditions, and ending the race in dry conditions again.
Tire wear is also a feature I really appreciate, which I find plays a significant role during races in F1 2015.
During races, I follow the crew chief’s race strategy; however, I have experienced situations where I feel like I can change the race strategy for a better race outcome, which is an immersive feeling that a race sim to offer sim racers.
F1 2015 includes a Pro Championship season that emphasizes realism for the sim racer. In Pro Championship mode, driving assists are turned off, race length is 100%, cockpit view is required, and disabled pitting help. I have not done a Pro Championship season yet; however, I look forward to this mode as I want as much realism as I am capable.
For me, the single worst part of F1 2015 is the inability to review results of previous races. A race standings page appears just once never to be seen again. A work-around is to take a screen shot of the race standing; however, this is not as convenient as if this feature is built into F1 2015.
The second worst part of F1 2015 are when the AI gets alongside of me and takes me out with an angry maneuver that defies physics. The angry AI maneuver is most annoying when it occurs when I get a blue flag and let the lapping car along side of me and in the blink of an eye I am wrecked into the wall/grass. It is hilarious to watch, but not fun to experience. The fix to this problem is to improve my racing ability so that I don’t get lapped, and the most effective fix is to stay in first from beginning to the end of the race.
- Dynamic weather
- Tire wear
- Pro Championship mode
- Immersive racing experience
- Inability to review past races during the same season
- AI can unfairly be angry at times to the detriment of the player

If you want to win, go way of the Tiger with an agility build. If you want to take longer to win than your base building sessions in Fallout 4, then by all means, pick the other two inferior paths.
I really want to like this game, because it's art style, music and call backs to 80 - 90's martial arts movies makes the game quite charming and enjoyable. It's a tragic shame that four severe factors corrodes this enjoyment:
1.The crippling stat decay system: training or not, your progress will drop by roughly 50 % everyday regardless.  Either the devs never exercised in their lives or they REALLY wanted to add micro payments in their game to mitigate this effect but were deathly afraid of having their small building burned to the ground.
2.Disappointing story for the champion path:  If you wanna play a hero, look elsewhere, because the game will punish you by eventually becoming a commercialized tool instead of a boxer and have a weak as heck ending to top it off. If this was supposed to be a nod to Rocky 3, then they nodded so hard, their nose busted on the counter.
3.RNG: Aside from picking your moves before the fight, you have no control of combat whatsoever, you have to pray to RNGesus that your fighter not only attacks, but follow up with more afterwards and not stare into his opponent's eyes likes he's falling in love.
4.Severe balance issues:  Like I said, if you want the less stressful path possible, then go agility, because having to hit and avoid damage is far more preferrable than taking hits as the RNG system screws you over because your fighter felt like taking hits than giving them, running out of stamina and eventually losing. The more strength you have the more tired you get, as stamina doesn't regenerate as much as it should, unless you have skills that increase your chances as you get up from the floor.
There is, of course the common complaint of repetiveness of going through your "simmy" routines, but if these four glaring issues were mostly addressed, I would of forgave this.  Unfortunately it only adds to the tedium of this game.
If you want to buy this game for the call backs and asthetics, I won't stop you, but you've have been warned.

78 minutes is all I could stand in Watch_Dogs (1), I didn't really plan on buying the second game for multiple reasons, the main one being Always on UPLAY and being bored out of my mind of Watch_Dogs(1). I hate the idea with a passion, I already have steam installed, why should I install another game manager.
But I watched a review and I heard these points: 1. Gadgets (flying drone, jumper drone) 2. The mood of the game (it's exactly opposite of Watch_Dogs (1). This game, for the most part, is colourful and happy. As a casual gamer, this is exactly what I want from a game. What I didn't want is GTAV and playing the game mostly with drones is more rewarding than expected.
I shot maybe 20 bullets in the entire game (and even that in the final missions, where droning was unexpectedly difficult, after stunning the guards, so they don't wake up).
I put in significant effort to avoid the online interactions and disabled everything I could in settings, however I did complete all the single player side missions, they're a great way to gain unlocks in abilities.
45 hours is what I got out of the base game(no dlc) and it didn't feel stale, I'd happily spend more time with it, if the dlcs were more clearly explained. I don't want to pay extra for skins/cars, but if there is a mission pack, I'd happily pay for it.
Couple of tips that made me really enjoy the game:
1. Buy the flying drone ASAP, don't spend money on anything, get it ASAP, it changes the game. I've completed countless missions without getting out of the car. Just drive up, use the flyer to scope and then the jumper to complete the mission. Then call back and drive off like a ghost, incredibly rewarding.
2. Get Gang War and Evidence forgin perks, the chaos caused by unleashing thugs and police on the guards that are blocking your way is a great cover to let you do what you want.
3. Dropping bombs/tazers from the flying drone is probably the most fun I've had in games for a very long time.
P.S. Yes, FPS drops are an issue (even at 1080p with a gtx1070 and a very beefy pc), Yes, the game isn't extremely stable, it crashed maybe 15-20 times during my 45 hours, many times signifying that I should stop playing and do something useful :)

I want to love this game, I really do, but it just keeps building up to a peak and then falling flat.
The aesthetic is great. Even though you are going to the same handful of places over and over again, they all have real charm to them. It begins to grate when you realise that everything is the same every single time you go there. Even having random characters moving in the scenes would help. The gym is the closest to getting it right, but the same people are on the same equipment every single time.
The music sounds good, but it really starts to grate after you've heard the one 'rocky' style loop for hours on end.
Storywise, the game starts off well, but it falls down pretty quickly. Characters are introduced with potential storylines, but the majority of characters are simply introduced and then used only to get various buffs. The story with the main love interest, for example, doesn't go anywhere. You may as well just use her to get a buff and then ignore her for four days! The ending is completely anti-climatic. The game just ends. No final fight. No closure.
The gameplay is a mix of RNG and tactical skill selection. Looking at the skill trees, you can imagine that you would need to cleverly select your skills and talents for the opponent you face, but you don't. Most fights are reliably won only by having equal or higher stats than your opponent, and the way the skill trees are arranged quickly becomes uninspiring.
Overall, if you like time management games, then you'll have fun. I enjoyed my time with the game, but I wouldn't recommend it over other titles.

Punch Club is a tough sell.  It's that management game you want to absolutely love, but end up scratching your head after.  Part lack of information and part "the entire game is backwards," Punch Club had me wanting more, but with a hope it'll be different.
You play a hard-up-on-life-and-not-very-smart stereotypical boxer that, for reasons unknown, lives in a city where the economy is absolute garbage.  Make money in the early game by jack-hammering for $50 in an 8 hour shift ($6.25/hour?!) to, in turn, spend $40 of it on two pieces of meat (yes, "meat") to restore your hunger for the day.  Later you end up giving $40 (or more) to your girlfriend to get her to leave you alone (aka: love you for the allowance).  The point being made here, is that the economy is extremely messed up and makes no game-balance sense.  In the late game, you're swimming in money, simply because it comes in daily and at this point: you have nothing to spend in on.
This is where my main complaint and reservation comes from Punch Club.  The entire game story is played backwards in terms of game balance.
The start of the game you have absolutely no money, no skills and no friends.  You spend your days training, working and fighting.  In order to train, you spend $10 to use the Gym (each entry; no monthly membership!) until you leave.  You can also buy gym equipment for your garage for a hefty fee of $100 to $300 each piece.  At the end of each day, some of your skills that you just trained, regress.  How great to earn '100 strength' only to lose 40 of it in a heartbeat.  Your fights earn you only experience at the start of the game, not even chump change.  You eventually are given the opportunity to street fight, which also earns you absolutely squat.  When presented the ability to fight in Ultimate fights (underground fight club), it
for money, but only $40 for a win or $20 on a loss.  All the while, you're spending what little money you earn from the two in-game side jobs toward on food to keep on training.  Bottom line, you're hard pressed to find cash to use including your couch cushions.
Then comes "late game," where you've finished the second league.  The entire game flips itself onto its head and pits you into a position where money means absolutely nothing.  All gym equipment is at your disposal, free of charge.  Food is put into your home every day without question.  Matches you fight in give you good money.  Eventually, you earn money daily, just for breathing.  All for what purpose?  This entire stage is focused on you grinding away at training with no distractions in order to become some form of champion, so money has extremely minimal impact on your game play (you may buy energy drinks and give your girlfriend 'go away' cash... and that's pretty much it).
The game is backwards.  It would have made far more sense if you started in a free gym to help train your lowly character, and put your meagre money toward food where in late game start to pay for more things when money became so readily available.  Instead this very weird "have absolutely nothing to have absolutely everything" pathway causes the early game to take far too many hours than it should and late game to be over so quick you didn't even realize that was the end of the game.
Punch Club itself, as a whole, could have been more fun without the unnecessary grind - it's important to note that without that grind, the game would have been two hours long.  The storyline acts as a distraction while the game takes away your hard earned training to prolong the ending.
Was it fun?  Absolutely.  Balance issues aside, watching your character get pit into tougher challenges with you having very little control over their actions is a great way to build player suspense, happiness and frustrations.  Unfortunately the "fun" is overshadowed by 80% of your time staring at orbs flying into the air due to the overall lack of game balance and story substance.

ROAD REDEMPTION. A much improved Early Access Experience
I originally reviewed this game in 2015 and gave it a bad review. At the time I appreciated that the game was very Early Access and could not recommend it.
So what has changed?
Well, in my original review I mentioned that there was no option for a quick race and at the time the game was distinctly lacking in certain areas. This now brings us to today's Early Access review. The game is still in Early Access state but has had significant updates from the developer. Included now is a Quick Race mode which is truly a welcome feature as many gamers would just like to have a couple of short blasts. I don't understand why every game these days just has to have a progression system but this game restricts it to the campaign mode only and I don't find it a grind like in many other games.
With regards to the overall gameplay; Road Redemption is very much it's own game. It certainly is not a spiritual successor to the classic Road Rash games and if, like I, you puurchase this game with the sole purpose of replicating that experience then you will be disappointed.
This game plays like a Mad Max on motorcycles. Pick your ride and lay wate in a post apocalyptic world of sorts. It is very much it's own game and needs to be appreciated that way.
The inclusion of full 4 player local split screen is a very welcome addition, this is a game that cries out to be played with friends and I am hoping for online multiplayer to become a feature very soon.
I must say that the devs have been very active in the community and I have had numerous messages exchanged with them regarding this game. This gives me a lot of encouragement that the game will be out of Early Access very soon and I am changing my original review from a negative to a positive.

...and this violence is understandably much worse in this modern day game (not in a bad way)... it has a decent amount of blood and a sort of disturbing sound effect when the melee weapon cracks against the body of an opponent.
